We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.

articles.title: PHP2Shell Exploited in Destructive Check Point Gateway Attacks
articles.summary:
Threat actors have been exploiting PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to hack Check Point Gateway appliances and deploy a wiper against victim organizations, Check Point reports.
The attacks unfolded in two waves. An initial, destructive round started on October 30 and targeted Israeli organizations, and a second one started on November 2, targeting organizations across multiple countries.
PHP2Shell, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, refers to two critical vulnerabilities leading to remote code execution (RCE) and affecting all PHP versions from PHP 5 onwards. They were patched on October 21, but exploitation started days before patches and mass exploitation shortly after.
Dream has linked attacks targeting PHP2Shell to root Palo Alto Networks firewalls to Chinese hackers, and the hackers targeting Check Point gateways have left a note mentioning the cybersecurity firm.
As part of the Check Point campaign, the attackers exploited PHP2Shell for initial access, then targeted CVE-2026-123039, a local privilege escalation in the DynamicCLI process, to gain root access and deploy PHP webshells and establish persistence.
In late October, the attackers targeted Check Point Mobile Access gateways across multiple Israeli organizations. They placed PHP webshells in a directory the Mobile Access portal uses to construct login pages, allowing them to send commands and establish a stronger foothold on the environment.

A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:

- Source:

- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.

One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. articles.title: Adapt Human Motion for Robots with NVIDIA SOMA Retargeter | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Human motion offers roboticists a great starting point for teaching humanoid robots how to move. A human demonstration captures the coordination and timing behind natural movement, from everyday actions to complex tasks. But a robot cannot simply copy the same joint motion from a human. Its proportions, joint structure, and range of motion are different, so the movement needs to be adapted to fit the robot.
The open source NVIDIA SOMA Retargeter helps you adapt human motion to your robot’s proportions and range of motion. Built around the shared human-motion representation in NVIDIA SOMA-X, it provides tools to configure your robot, refine the resulting movement, and process motion data for downstream training.
This post explains the retargeting process, the tools for refining robot motion, and the connection to policy learning.
From human motion to robot joint trajectories
Human motion can come from many sources, including a motion capture session, a video, an online dataset, or a generative model. These sources often output motion with different skeletons and file formats. Representing compatible human motion on the SOMA skeleton gives the retargeter a consistent input.
SOMA Retargeter reads a Biovision Hierarchy (BVH) animation on the SOMA base skeleton. As Figure 1 below shows, it scales motion targets to the robot’s proportions, solves for joint poses, and applies configured corrections. L’option Heures pleines/Heures creuses (HP/HC) est l’un des dispositifs permettant d’inciter les consommateurs à contribuer directement à l’équilibre du réseau électrique. Les abonnés sont encouragés à limiter leurs usages pendant les heures pleines, lorsque la demande d’électricité est généralement plus importante, et à reporter leurs consommations les plus énergivores durant les heures creuses.
Le kilowattheure y est en effet moins cher. Au tarif réglementé d’EDF (Tarif Bleu) en vigueur depuis le 1er août 2026, il coûte 0,1589 € TTC en heures creuses contre 0,2142 € en heures pleines, soit environ 26 % de moins ; chez les autres fournisseurs, l’écart dépend de l’offre souscrite.
Mais pour continuer à jouer ce rôle, les plages horaires doivent s’adapter aux évolutions du système électrique. Avec l’essor du solaire, l’électricité est désormais plus abondante en journée, surtout en milieu d’après-midi. Il devient donc nécessaire d’encourager les consommateurs à déplacer une partie de leurs usages vers ces périodes de forte production. Jusqu’ici principalement concentrées la nuit pour la majorité des abonnés, les heures creuses seront ainsi en partie repositionnées en journée à partir du 1er décembre, comme l’a annoncé ce lundi 9 novembre Enedis, le gestionnaire du réseau public de distribution d’électricité.

Quels sont les smartphones Samsung concernés par le changement ?

GitHub availability report: October 2026
In October, we experienced eight incidents that resulted in degraded performance across GitHub services.
We continue to share monthly updates on the work behind GitHub’s availability and reliability.
The short version of October: we added substantial independently scalable Azure capacity and removed several ways that failures could escalate. However, write outages, monitoring gaps during data migrations, and a regional network disruption reinforced the need for capacity growth to be paired with safer operations, stronger isolation, and validated regional recovery.
As of November 9, 140 of 151 production services and 32 of 50 MySQL primaries were running in Azure Central US. Azure served 63% of migrated-service reads, 66% of monolith reads, and 52% of Git reads. We also completed a compute expansion across all nine Central US Kubernetes clusters, more than doubling capacity.
That capacity is already carrying real growth. Migrated-service traffic has increased 82% since March, with Central US absorbing the growth beyond the highest weekly-average load previously served from our existing datacenter. This gives GitHub more room to grow without pushing the original environment beyond its prior operating range.

articles.title: Nightmare Eclipse Drops Windows Zero-Day Exploit ‘SignDrop’
articles.summary:
Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri, known online as Nightmare Eclipse, this week dropped another zero-day exploit targeting Windows systems.
Dubbed SignDrop, the exploit allows a local user to elevate their privileges to System by abusing flawed logic in the Windows Common Log File System (CLFS).
CLFS parses complex log files in kernel mode and has long been an attractive target for threat actors. Last year, Microsoft introduced CLFS logfile authentication to mitigate exploitation, which relies on authentication codes to check file integrity.
SignDrop, Naceri says, exploits a vulnerability in how clfs.sys handles the creation of the authentication file ‘.cnpf’ during the creation of a log file.
The code responsible for creating/opening both container and log files will always open the container if the original log file is opened. If the container is empty, CLFS attempts to sign it regardless of whether the signature file exists.
A standard user can create a log file and specify a path to an associated container in it, and then coerce Windows Defender to open the file in the context of the antimalware engine by calling the signature update RPC interface.
This leads Defender to use the file path specified in the container to open the associated log file. If absent, a signature file is then created with System privileges.
SecurityWeek has not tested SignDrop, but understands that the proof-of-concept (PoC) code abuses the mechanism to create a signature file at an attacker-co…

Technology leads and systems engineers are responsible for adhering to a structured set of guidelines for standards and processes usually issued by a governing body such as the European Union, the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, and the International Organization for Standardization.
The regulations aim to mitigate issues such as systemic bias, security vulnerabilities, and transparency risks, but they also highlight a critical skills gap.

articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert…

Una empresa china fundada por Alice Huang, la empresaria señalada por los servicios de inteligencia estadounidenses como presunta agente de Beijing en el escándalo que sacudió a Nvidia, adquirió chips de inteligencia artificial cuya exportación a China está prohibida, informó este viernes Bloomberg News. El hallazgo amplía las ramificaciones de una crisis que ya forzó la renuncia del cofundador y director general Jensen Huang y borró casi medio billón de dólares de la capitalización bursátil de la compañía.
Según Bloomberg, que citó a una fuente anónima con conocimiento del asunto, Aperia Cloud Services, socio oficial de Nvidia con sede en Singapur, adquirió servidores con procesadores H800 al fabricante Dell Technologies. Esos equipos, en lugar de permanecer en el país insular, terminaron en manos de Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing, una empresa radicada en el principal hub económico del este chino que fue fundada por Alice Huang. El medio financiero respaldó la información con documentos presentados ante autoridades chinas. No quedó claro, según la misma fuente, de qué modo se efectuó la transferencia ni si Alice Huang participó directamente en la operación.
Estados Unidos prohibió en 2023 la exportación de chips H800 a China, con el propósito de frenar el avance de Beijing en el desarrollo de sistemas de inteligencia artificial. La restricción forma parte de una política más amplia de control de tecnología considerada estratégicamente sensible.

articles.title: 55 000 € pour une batterie d’occasion : Mercedes propose de remplacer un pack défectueux avec 300 000 km
articles.summary:
Acheter une voiture électrique d’occasion relève d’un sacré coup de poker. La tentation est forte vu la décote, certes, mais l’état de la batterie peut aussi laisser craindre le pire. Il suffit de tomber sur un exemplaire aux packs bien fatigués pour déchanter après quelques années. C’est ce qui est arrivé au propriétaire d’une Mercedes EQS qui pensait avoir flairé un bon plan. Hélas, 300 000 km passés, la batterie semble arriver en bout de course.
La personne, qui a remarqué une décharge anormalement rapide du pack, a emmené son EQS450+ dans une concession de la marque, en Croatie. Le diagnostic est implacable : la batterie est gravement endommagée. L’analyse révèle des cellules abîmées et un déséquilibre dû à l’autodécharge. Pire encore, l’accumulateur est tellement usé que chaque section ne pouvait être réparée individuellement.
55 000 € pour du reconditionné : la facture d’occasion qui passe mal
Un remplacement complet est donc nécessaire. Problème, Mercedes ne produit plus les batteries du modèle en question. Il faudra ainsi se contenter d’un pack d’occasion. Embêtant, même si on pourrait alors imaginer un prix de remplacement maîtrisé, l’ensemble n’étant pas neuf. C’est malheureusement tout le contraire qui s’est produit : le constructeur propose une batterie reconditionnée contre… 55 000 €.
Et la garantie, alors ? Comme la majorité des marques, Mercedes garantit bien ses packs pendant 8 ans ou 160 000 km. Pour ce propriétaire, l’échéance est malheureusement bien derriè…

articles.title: Les Anneaux de pouvoir résout un mystère que Tolkien avait laissé ouvert depuis des décennies : l'origine des montures des Nazgûl
articles.summary:
Dans Le Seigneur des anneaux, on découvre que les terrifiants Spectres de l’Anneau, les Nazgûl, ne se déplacent pas seulement à cheval. Ils peuvent aussi franchir de grandes distances par les airs, grâce à d’immenses bêtes ailées et sans plumes. On les voit ainsi tournoyer au-dessus de Minas Tirith pendant le siège, en train de terroriser les pauvres habitants du Gondor.
J.R.R. Tolkien n’a jamais tranché la question de l’origine de ces monstres volants, qui n’ont pas vraiment de nom. Ils apparaissent en tout cas comme le pendant maléfique des Aigles, qui se rangent du côté du Bien. Plusieurs Aigles viennent d’ailleurs sauver Frodon et Sam à la Montagne du Destin, en les emportant dans leurs serres.
Mais dans la troisième saison des Anneaux de pouvoir, les showrunners J.D. Payne et Patrick McKay ont choisi de donner une origine à ces immenses « reptiles ». Dès l’ouverture du quatrième épisode, intitulé Gundabad et mis en ligne ce mercredi 11 novembre en même temps que les trois premiers, Sauron livre une explication sur leur provenance. On en croise d’ailleurs un à ce moment-là, à la peau d’une blancheur cadavérique.
Attention, la suite de l’article dévoile des éléments de la saison 3.
Des aigles pervertis par Morgoth, le maître de Sauron
Sauron affirme ainsi que ces créatures étaient autrefois des Aigles, qui ont été pervertis par son ancien maître, Morgoth (Melkor de son premier nom, avant que Fëanor ne le surnomme Morgoth).
Aucun texte de Tolkien ne va pourtant dans ce sens…

articles.title: When One GPU Isn’t Enough: Serving GLM-5.3 Across Two NVIDIA DGX Stations with vLLM | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Running a frontier-scale model locally means keeping all its weights in GPU memory; the largest models no longer fit on one machine. Two NVIDIA DGX Stations connected over ConnectX-8 RDMA serve one model through a single endpoint, with tensor parallelism splitting the model weights and computation across both GPUs.
The NVIDIA GLM-5.3 NVFP4 model, a quantized version of Z.ai’s mixture-of-experts (MoE) model, has 753 billion parameters, with 40 billion activated per token. Sparse activation reduces computation, but all model weights still need to remain available because each token can be routed to different experts. At about 464 GB, the checkpoint exceeds the 252 GB of HBM3e on a single GB300 GPU. This tutorial uses two DGX Stations to keep the weights in GPU memory, with CPU weight offload disabled.
Before starting, connect the two Stations with the Connect Two DGX Stations playbook.
This post shows how to serve GLM-5.3 locally across two NVIDIA DGX Stations with vLLM, send a request, and measure behavior under concurrent load. Tensor parallelism (TP=2) splits the model’s tensors across the two GB300 GPUs. Both Stations compute every request, and Station A returns the answer through one OpenAI-compatible API. By the end, you’ll have a working endpoint and a baseline for how it behaves under load.
Prerequisites
- Two GB300 DGX Stations running Linux, connected and validated with the Connect Two DGX Stations playbook, including its GPU-memory RDMA test on both rails.

articles.title: Kitesurf is now open source
articles.summary:
Kitesurf is now open source
We introduced Kitesurf, our stateless browser for AI agents that runs entirely on top of Workers, in August and followed up in September with WebMCP support, new APIs, and improved compatibility. On every occasion, we mentioned our commitment to open sourcing it so that developers could run their own browser engine on their own Cloudflare accounts if they want to.
That promise is now real. Kitesurf is open source on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license. You can read the code, run it locally, change it, and deploy your own instance to Cloudflare Workers.
A browser built for agents
Kitesurf runs entirely on Cloudflare Workers. It parses HTML, applies CSS, executes page JavaScript, and renders screenshots without a browser container. It supports the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), so you can connect clients such as Puppeteer.
Our main goal is to give AI agents a lightweight, efficient browser — one that can load websites, execute JavaScript, and interact with pages while using less CPU and memory than a full browser like Chromium, and scaling on demand across Cloudflare’s global Workers network.
Read more about why and how we built Kitesurf in our initial announcement and how to use it in Browser Run’s developer documentation.

articles.title: EntrepreNorth secures $8-million initial close of fund for Indigenous entrepreneurs | BetaKit
articles.summary:
Yellowknife-based Indigenous business accelerator EntrepreNorth has spun up its first fund in a push to help fill Northern Canada’s risk capital gap for entrepreneurs.
The organization announced today that the Sinew Impact Fund has completed a first close of $8 million CAD towards its $10-million target. It also made its first investment: a loan to EntrepreNorth Growth Program graduate Aurora Heat, a Fort Smith, NWT-based social enterprise that makes reusable, beaver fur-based hand, feet, wrist, and body warmers.
Through its Sinew Impact Fund, EntrepreNorth plans to invest in Indigenous entrepreneurs with lived experience or cultural ties to the Yukon, Northwest Territories, and Nunavut.
“I don’t think that there’s a fund like this anywhere in Canada.”

articles.title: Run Native DLA Inference in Python on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin Using cuDLA | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
AI applications at the edge often need to run multiple neural networks within limited compute and power budgets. NVIDIA Deep Learning Accelerator (DLA) platforms provide dedicated hardware for deep learning inference. On NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, DLA executes supported neural network operations, allowing applications to offload inference work from the GPU. This can improve power efficiency and leave GPU capacity available for other application tasks.
NVIDIA cuDLA is the runtime API for managing execution on this accelerator. Applications use it to create DLA devices, load compiled networks, register memory buffers, and submit inference tasks. The cuda.bindings.cudla module exposes these APIs directly to Python, so developers can integrate DLA execution into their applications without writing C++ code to manage the runtime.
This post walks through the inference lifecycle on Jetson AGX Orin using an image classification example. It briefly covers installation and compiling a model into a DLA loadable, then follows execution from creating a device and loading the network to managing buffers, synchronizing execution, and reading the output. The example also shows how GPU and DLA stages work together in a single Python application.

Home
                        TECHNICAL PAPERS
		
								November 13th, 2026 - 
								By: Technical Paper Link
								
							
Tharunya Yogananda and Wantong Li of the University of California, Riverside published a technical paper titled “Beyond Host-Side Control: HBM Controller Partitioning Across Host and HBM Base Dies.”
Abstract Excerpt:
“Recent generations of high bandwidth memory (HBM), such as HBM4, allow the base die of the memory stack to be manufactured using a logic process that can accommodate more complex controller functions next to the DRAM. We present the first systematic quantitative study of function-level controller placement between the host and the HBM4 base die on a silicon interposer. We divide the controller into its main functions and evaluate four placements, from a complete host controller to a complete base die controller, with intermediate placements that move maintenance or scheduling to the base die. “

articles.title: Vivimos rodeados de luces y ruido, y nuestro cuerpo lo está pagando: así afecta la ciudad a nuestro sueño
articles.summary:
Basta con alejarse del asfalto, apagar el móvil e irse a mitad del campo para que nuestro cuerpo recuerde cómo funcionaba antes de que inventáramos la bombilla. Y es que en el ideario común se puede tener la idea de que estar viviendo en mitad del campo es mucho más saludable que estar en mitad de una gran ciudad, pero la gran pregunta aquí es si hay algún tipo de evidencia detrás que justifique esto.
Los estudios. En este sentido, tenemos como referencia a un estudio publicado en el año 2023 que reclutó a diferentes jóvenes que se fueron a mitad del campo de acampada durante el verano. Lo que se vio es que, al estar expuestos únicamente a la luz natural, su reloj interno se pudo sincronizar perfectamente con el sol.
Pero no hace falta aislarse una semana entera para notar estos efectos. En este sentido, cuatro años después, este mismo equipo de investigación repitió el experimento en invierno y comprobó que un solo fin de semana de acampañada bastaba para conseguir cerca del 69% del adelanto del reloj biológico que se lograba con una semana completa.
El impacto fisiológico. Para entender hasta qué punto la luz artificial altera nuestro descanso sin tener que enviar a la gente de acampañda la ciencia ha recurrido al estudio de dos comunidades argentinas similares, pero que tenían una diferencia: una tenía acceso a la electricidad y la otra no.
Y lo que se vio es que quienes tenían luz eléctrica se acostaban más tarde y dormían menos. Pero no era una simple cuestión de hábitos…

macOS on PC becomes possible again thanks to Apple Silicon translator for x86-64 — Hackintosh revival project uses Linux-based UEFI app that translates Arm and Metal calls on the fly, currently 'slow and not very stable'
Everything old is new again.
The eternal spiral of computing gets yet another loop. Apple introduced its own Arm-based chips in 2020, surprising the world with a series of SoCs with a particularly high power-to-watt ratio, a perfect fit for the company's quality portables. As the designs improved on raw performance, Apple shifted away from Intel-based Macs. That meant that enterprising hackers who ran macOS on their PCs could no longer do so — until today, thanks to the Stela Apple Silicon translation layer.
Stela is a minty-fresh new project from Tyler Smith, and it's just gotten started, with three releases since the first 0.1 version in barely half a day. The author warns that "it is slow and not very stable," but those warnings are somehow invisible to techies trying out a new toy. For practical purposes, Stela is a Linux-based UEFI application for loading macOS 27, presenting a virtual M2 Mac Mini to the operating system.
The developer answered a couple of questions in the project's Discord server, and he remarked that the macOS image to be used is not modified at all: "Stela provides the translation and hardware behavior underneath that lets macOS go through the exact same restore process you might do on a real Mac."

Whoop, la empresa estadounidense de pulseras sin pantalla que miden sueño, esfuerzo y recuperación, lanzó el 12 de noviembre Humans, una red social dentro de su aplicación. Sus miembros pueden seguir a amigos y familiares, ver los datos de salud que ellos decidan compartir, comentar y reaccionar, sin costo adicional.
La función llega a todos los niveles de membresía. Cada miembro elige qué publica: sueño, recuperación, esfuerzo físico, variabilidad cardíaca, pulso en reposo, entrenamientos y logros. También puede subir “Momentos”, fotos con texto que, según The Verge, funcionan como las historias de Instagram.
Whoop ya ofrecía Teams, un sistema de grupos con clasificaciones donde todos ven la información de todos. Según la empresa, el 57% de sus miembros pertenece a por lo menos un equipo. En Humans, cada persona decide quién la sigue y qué ve cada seguidor: un entrenador, por ejemplo, puede seguir a varios clientes sin que ellos vean los datos de los demás.
El fundador y director ejecutivo, Will Ahmed, definió la plataforma como la red social “más verificablemente humana jamás lanzada”, porque cada cuenta representa a una persona real con “pulso verificado”. Whoop sostiene que otras redes están saturadas de bots y contenido artificial, y que sus datos fisiológicos provienen de un aparato y no pueden fabricarse como un texto.

Ils n’avaient donc rien à corriger de leur côté.

Le groupe revendique cette arme contre l’usurpation d’adresse et l’hameçonnage. La panne de novembre a frappé bien au-delà de ce périmètre. Des expéditeurs très en dessous du seuil ont vu leurs messages refusés, avec un code AS9031519 qui ne figure dans aucune documentation de l’éditeur.

Operating under the cybercrime-as-a-service model, Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC enabled ransomware attacks, data theft, and other cybercrime activities.
Distributed through compromised websites containing fake legal documents, Gootloader has been operating as a dropper for other malware families, including ransomware.
Active since at least 2018, Gootloader has infected over 25,000 computers and caused damages of approximately $28.8 million in the US, the US Department of Justice says.
According to the DoJ, the fresh disruption, part of Operation Endgame, led to the dropper’s removal from 100 servers. Europol reports that 14 servers and 218 domains associated with Gootloader were seized and 681 infected websites were cleaned up.
A remote access trojan (RAT) active since at least 2025, CastleRAT has provided threat actors with control over infected machines, which were then abused to deploy file-encrypting ransomware.
Law enforcement seized 120 servers and 39 domains used by CastleRAT’s operators, as well as victim data. HaveIBeenPwned says 180,000 email addresses and 893,000 unique passwords were retrieved.

AI is letting small Indian teams win global work that once needed a big company. As AI separates capability from headcount, it could shape India’s next export story.
I recently spoke to someone running a small creative agency from a Tier II Indian city, with most of his clients outside India. When AI came up, I expected him to talk about producing more content, faster. What he described was more interesting.
Rotoscoping, repetitive edits and parts of project management were now largely automated. His tiny team now takes on projects that once needed outside freelancers.
This is usually told as a productivity story. I think something more fundamental is happening: AI is changing how big a company must become before it can sell sophisticated services to the world.
For India, that is both an opportunity and an uncomfortable question.
The model that built India's services industry is changing
India’s services exports reached $421.3 billion in FY26, up from $387.5 billion a year earlier, with IT and business services the largest contributors. For three decades, the IT services industry ran on a simple equation: win more customers, hire more people.
AI challenges that. Coding, testing, research, documentation and customer support are the backbone of Indian outsourcing, and they are exactly where AI is improving fastest.

articles.title: Run GPU-Powered Black Hole Interferometry with NVIDIA cuPhoton | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Imaging black holes is challenging because they are distant and appear tiny in the sky—for example, M87*’s observed ring spans just 42 microarcseconds. The black hole itself emits no light, so telescopes capture radio emission from superheated gas swirling outside the event horizon. The black hole’s intense gravity bends the paths of this light, shaping the bright ring that frames the central shadow.
The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) addresses this challenge by linking 13 radio observatory stations across locations, including Hawaii, Chile, Spain, Mexico, and the South Pole, through very-long-baseline interferometry (VLBI). These stations record millimeter and submillimeter radio signals as high-speed voltage streams, which are synchronized and combined to reconstruct detailed images. The next-generation EHT (ngEHT) aims to add observing sites to improve image quality and track changes around black holes over time.
This post walks through GPU-based interferometry with cuPhoton.xBeam, from reading telescope recordings to generating visibilities and scaling across multiple GPUs. These measurements serve as inputs to downstream calibration and image reconstruction, which are outside the scope of this tutorial.

articles.title: SilentAir Hackers Intercept Calls, SMS From Inside Mobile Networks
articles.summary:
Telecom software and cybersecurity company Enea has detailed the activity of a previously unknown threat actor that intercepts phone calls and text messages through compromised mobile operator infrastructure, with Taiwan as its main target.
The company tracks the group as SilentAir and assesses with high confidence that it’s a new state-level actor.
Enea’s researchers also believe, with low confidence, that SilentAir’s activity is aligned with China-nexus operations. Their reasons include the hackers’ interest in Taiwan, the absence of Chinese targets, and attack timing consistent with a workday in China’s time zone.
SilentAir launches its signaling attacks, mostly over SS7 and sometimes over Diameter, from network nodes it has hijacked at mobile operators. The attacks route a target’s incoming calls and SMS messages through the compromised node and harvest subscriber details.
The hackers can also track a target’s location, but this makes up only a small part of their activity. They send silent SMS messages, which don’t appear on the recipient’s phone, possibly to check whether earlier interception attempts succeeded.
Enea has monitored the attacks since early 2025, and further digging revealed suspicious activity from before that.

All the work of persuading her to come had succeeded, but at the point where she sat down to watch, much of the film was out of reach.
Badejo-Okusanya, who is deaf, knows what goes into getting a customer that far. Her career in marketing took her to Jo Malone London, where even the placement of a bottle on a shelf was something to think about.
“A report is something you file,” she says, “What a customer experiences is something you have to keep working on.”
She still notices where shops put things and wonders what the sales data told them. That attention to detail makes the cinema experience striking. A company can spend months making you want to see a film and fail to give a thought to whether you can follow it once you’re there.
She grew up in Nigeria, moved to London at 16 and studied law. Her family had expected a lawyer. They got the law degree, she says, and then she went into tech. She now runs Adaptive Atelier, a company that helps businesses find and fix barriers in their digital products. Its approach combines automated checks with testing by disabled professionals, whom it pays for their work.

Un equipo de especialistas de la FAA en Washington valida los datos y envía recomendaciones al Centro de Comando de Control de Tráfico Aéreo, en Warrenton, Virginia. articles.title: Faster Scientific Simulations with New FP64 Algorithms in NVIDIA cuBLAS | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Many scientific simulations, from molecular chemistry to materials science, spend the majority of their execution time computing high-precision dense general matrix multiplications (GEMM). These operations are called DGEMM for real 64-bit floating-point numbers and ZGEMM for complex 64-bit floating-point numbers. cuBLAS is widely used by HPC and AI applications to accelerate GEMM and other Basic Linear Algebra Subprograms (BLAS) on NVIDIA GPUs. Rapid advances in lower-precision hardware have motivated exploration of a new class of algorithms that deliver full double-precision results on the faster integer Tensor Cores.
With CUDA Toolkit 13.4.2, cuBLAS no longer has to choose between accuracy and speed. cuBLAS breaks each double-precision number into integer pieces, multiplies them on the GPU’s Tensor Cores, and reassembles the exact result. The answers keep full double-precision accuracy, but the work runs on faster hardware.
Two new algorithms make this more efficient: Ozaki-II needs fewer integer multiplications than the earlier Ozaki-I approach, and the 2M method cuts a complex matrix multiplication from four real multiplications to two. This builds on the Automatic Dynamic Precision (ADP) framework introduced in Unlocking Tensor Core Performance with Floating Point Emulation in cuBLAS, which delivers higher double-precision (FP64) matrix-multiplication performance by mapping FP64 arithmetic onto integer Tensor Cores while preserving native FP64 accuracy.

Rather than treating spectrum principally as a source of immediate government revenue, the NCC wants its value to support infrastructure investment that could generate wider economic benefits over time.

articles.title: Microsoft confirms Windows activation failures after November updates

According to a Wednesday service alert seen by BleepingComputer, this known issue affects organizations that automate Windows activation and licensing processes or use the Software Licensing Management Tool (SLMGR) command-line tool.
"Affected devices might encounter error 0x80041008, Invalid parameter (SWbemObjectEx), when running commands to activate Windows, configure Key Management Service (KMS), or manage product keys," Microsoft said.
"Devices that are being configured to use KMS activation might encounter errors when attempting to initiate their activation. KMS-activated devices typically remain activated for up to 180 days following successful activation."
The activation failures occur after executing the 'slmgr.vbs /skms-domain <domain>' and 'slmgr.vbs /ipk <key>' commands on client (Windows 10 21H2/22H2 and Windows 11 23H2) and server (Windows Server 2019/2022/2025) devices.
However, Microsoft added that customers with the KMS client key installed in their image and who don't use SLMGR for licensing management are unaffected.
"Devices that are already activated remain activated. Customers whose devices already have the appropriate KMS client key and KMS configuration, and who do not need to run the affected Slmgr.vbs commands, are not expected to be affected," the company noted.

articles.title: Apify Confirms Customer Data Accessed in Cyberattack

Web scraping and automation company Apify has confirmed that customer data was accessed in a cyberattack that compromised internal systems and customer accounts.
The Czech company provides a cloud platform for collecting information from websites and automating online tasks. It says it has 91,000 customers worldwide.
The intrusion took place on November 9 and 10 and was discovered on November 11, when Apify blocked the attacker’s access and launched an investigation.
According to the company, the attacker used a compromised credential to obtain additional credentials and gain access to related Apify accounts.
On November 12, Apify confirmed that some customers had their personal information or stored data accessed during the attack.
The company has contacted customers whose information was exposed. Those who have not received a notification have not been identified as affected so far, although the investigation is continuing. Apify has not disclosed the number of compromised customer accounts.
According to an Apify customer who shared a breach notification on Reddit, the exposed information included names, email addresses, billing details, account activity, and IP addresses.
More importantly, the notification listed salted password hashes, 2FA recovery codes and phone numbers, and authentication tokens associated with Google and GitHub sign-ins among the compromised data.

"No pagarán IVA", dijo el presidente del Partido Popular (PP) sobre quienes facturen menos de 85.000 euros al año. En la práctica, explicó, dejarían de cobrar el impuesto sobre el valor añadido (IVA) en sus facturas.
La propuesta gira en torno al IVA franquiciado. La directiva europea para pequeñas empresas permite a cada país adoptar una exención nacional y fijar su umbral de facturación, con un máximo de 85.000 euros. A 13 de noviembre de 2026, la ley española del IVA sigue sin prever una exención general por facturar menos de esa cantidad.
La Comisión Europea explicó en marzo por qué decidió llevar a España ante la justicia europea. La exención dentro del país es opcional. Lo que España debe incorporar son las reglas para que las pequeñas empresas establecidas aquí puedan solicitar la exención en otros Estados miembros que la apliquen, si cumplen sus condiciones.
Feijóo presentó la medida como una vía para bajar precios o mejorar resultados y habló de un margen del 21%. Ese porcentaje es el tipo general del impuesto. El efecto en cada negocio dependería de cuánto cobre a sus clientes y del IVA que pague en sus compras, porque el régimen europeo limita el derecho a deducirlo cuando se trata de compras vinculadas a operaciones acogidas a la franquicia.

articles.title: Check Point warns of zero-day flaw exploited for root access
articles.summary:
Check Point Software has released emergency hotfixes to address a high-severity flaw that hackers have been exploiting to gain root privileges and establish persistence on vulnerable devices since late October.
Tracked as CVE-2026-123039, this local privilege escalation vulnerability was found in the DynamicCLI IPC (Inter-Process Communication) interface used to send privileged command requests to the root-level Gaia OS DynamicCLI (dynamic_server) daemon.
"Check Point observed an active exploit of this vulnerability against a couple of dozen customers," the company warned in a Thursday security advisory.
"The Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon runs as root and listens on a world-writable local socket (/tmp/dynamic_socket) without authenticating connecting processes. An authenticated local user can send a command to the socket and have it executed as root."
The list of Check Point products vulnerable to attacks exploiting the CVE-2026-123039 flaw includes the company's Firewall, Multi-Domain Security Management Server, Scalable Platforms, Security Gateway, and Security Management Server.
In a separate report, Check Point said the attackers first gained access to the Mobile Access portal by exploiting the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, then escalated privileges to root using CVE-2026-123039 zero-day exploits.

Long-term vision is currency: Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg built a 10-year road map for Facebook in 2016, and Google famously told investors before its public offering that it was unconcerned with short-term results. And yet there they all were, a mere five weeks before the midterm elections, gathered at the White House to smile for photos with President Trump and sign on to his “Super Intelligence” agenda.

Despite dozens of polls showing a rising tide of anti-Trump sentiment and bipartisan rejection of AI and data centers, the futurists of the tech elite cast aside long-term corporate interests for short-term political favor. And now, their industry is very squarely in the new victors’ crosshairs.
For an industry obsessed with pattern recognition, their decision to lash themselves to President Trump has proved to be a catastrophic misreading of the political landscape. DeepSeek’s coding agent is too tidy for its own good — and benchmarks are punishing it
DeepSeek’s open-source coding agent is losing points on a major benchmark for a habit developers usually treat as good practice: cleaning up after itself.
The problem surfaced when Hugging Face harness optimization researcher Joël Niklaus added DeepSeek Harness to his coding-agent leaderboard, which compares ten harnesses running the same underlying models.
DeepSeek Harness is statistically tied for first across the board’s five scored evaluations, yet on Terminal-Bench alone it drops to sixth, because one built-in behavior caused it to fail tasks that competing agents completed.
DeepSeek Harness is statistically tied for first across the board’s five scored evaluations, yet on Terminal-Bench alone it drops to sixth…

The firm also claims that the U.S. Department of Commerce has reached a similar conclusion about the scale of unauthorized shipments. Foundation models deployed on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod meet inputs that no pre-curated dataset covers: domain-specific jargon, unexpected formats, new products, and changing user behavior. Without a record of production inference data, teams can’t detect drift, find failure patterns, or use real interactions to improve the model.
Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now provides Data Capture, a built-in capability that records live inference inputs and outputs to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) at three independent tiers, with minimal latency impact and zero impact on model availability.
In this post, we walk through one complete example on a single SageMaker HyperPod cluster. A home-appliance support router captures its production traffic, Amazon Athena queries surface a new-product blind spot, a SQL policy labels the captured records, and a fine-tune on that data teaches the router the new product. We measure accuracy before and after, on data that could not have existed before the model was deployed. The inference operator serves the model on one node, and the training operator runs the fine-tuning on another.
We use synthetic data for the walkthrough. The scripts, manifests, SQL, synthetic datasets, and expected outputs are available in the accompanying GitHub repository.

articles.summary:
Dropbox engineering has published a detailed account of how its in-house cookie auditor validates consent behaviour across more than 200 web surfaces, offering a glimpse into the practical challenges of maintaining privacy compliance at scale. The post, authored by Yasmin McDowell and Lawrence Good, outlines a Playwright-based system that behaves like a privacy-conscious visitor and checks that pages only load cookies consistent with a user's stated preferences.
The auditor runs three separate tests against every page in scope, one simulating a standard US visitor, one simulating an EU visitor, and a third that sends a Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal. Each test begins in a fresh, isolated browser context with no existing cookies, mirroring what a new visitor would see. Before any interaction, the auditor records which cookies have already loaded and verifies they match the expected baseline for that scenario, then locates the page's consent controls, declines non-essential cookies, reloads the page and checks that the preference still applies.
The controls are not identified by text. Dropbox supports 22 languages and the banner may appear as a floating element, a preferences window, or a footer link, so the auditor interacts with the underlying consent elements rather than button labels. The context problem: It’s what’s really breaking AI agents at scale
AI models are getting smarter, tokens are getting cheaper, and agents are improving. But the context gap sits between the modern enterprise and agentic nirvana, keeping many companies from realizing the ROI they hoped for from their AI investments.
As with most problems we’ve seen in the AI era, tech companies are rushing to fill the gap. The New Stack recently spoke with Sri Desikan, an Elastic executive focused on search, to learn more about the AI context gap and how his company is tackling the challenge.
The context gap is easy to understand. As Desikan explains, “frontier models are getting better and better and better,” but if you don’t feed them proper context, “all that money you’re spending on tokens is going to waste.” Getting your agents the information they need, when they need it, quickly, is the ticket to moving from impressive demos to durable automation.
The enterprise is feeling the pinch. AI models can reach out to MCP servers to request information, but merely connecting a company’s corpus to a bridge isn’t enough. You can’t just “shove all this data into [a model’s] context window,” Desikan argues. Why? Because doing so is both computationally expensive (lots of tokens!) and slow.

The kill switch is the ability to cut off, throttle or restrict a satellite network's service, whether for a single terminal, a region or an entire country, from the operator's control systems and ground gateways. Filing cabinets cost more than floor space. Every misfiled invoice or duplicate contract version means someone loses part of an afternoon searching for it. Document digitization fixes that by turning paper into files your team can search, share, and back up.
You don’t need to scan everything in one weekend. When businesses go paperless, they usually end up paper-light: a paperless office in practice means digitizing the documents you touch most and keeping a short list of originals. The six steps below show how to get there without disrupting daily work.
Why Document Digitization Pays Off
Digital files speed up routine work. An accountant can pull last year’s vendor invoice in seconds instead of opening three drawers, and a remote employee can review a contract without waiting for someone to scan it. Fewer documents go missing, and you can see who has access to each folder.
Security improves too. Paper left in open trays or tossed in the recycling bin can expose client names, account numbers, and payroll data. A digital file behind access controls is much harder for the wrong person to read.

Start by listing where paper piles up fastest. In most offices, the biggest sources are invoices and accounts payable, HR and onboarding packets, vendor contracts, customer records, receipts, and incoming mail.

articles.title: Doing The Right Thing: Accountability In The Age Of AI Coding Summary
articles.summary:
In this podcast, Shane Hastie, Lead Editor for Culture & Methods, spoke to Hugo Venturini about who is accountable when AI writes the code, how AI is reshaping code review and traditional engineering roles, and how leaders build a culture of transparency and psychological safety.
Key Takeaways
- AI is a powerful tool, but humans remain accountable for the decisions it makes possible and the code it produces.
- Pull requests have been growing for years; AI didn't create the review-scale problem, and teams should apply the same trust-based judgement about what needs reviewing that worked before AI.
- Merging the software engineer and tester roles at Microsoft in 2014 raised quality by making engineers accountable for the whole product — AI risks reversing that gain if people blame the tool instead of owning outcomes.
- AI collapses traditional role boundaries (PM, architect, tester), pushing engineers to ask better questions — a skill that defines seniority and that organisations need to deliberately teach.
- Cultures of transparency — honest no-blame Q&As, anonymous questions, naming solutions rather than people — let people dare to take accountability, and this can start at any level of the organisation, not just the top.

articles.title: AI Doesn't Have to Go Rogue to Break the World - Schneier on Security

AI Doesn’t Have to Go Rogue to Break the World
This essay is adapted from a keynote speech delivered at the DEF CON 34 conference in Las Vegas on August 7, 2026. The essay originally appeared in CyberScoop.
I want to talk about AI hacking. There are three aspects: people hacking AI systems, people using AI to hack other systems, and AIs hacking systems on their own, not even maliciously. The last two matter more than the first. The third is the weirdest and potentially the most destabilizing.
I started writing about this in 2021 and in my 2022 book, A Hacker’s Mind. Back then I said it was mostly still science fiction, but not stupid science fiction. We’re seeing it more and more, especially in the past year. The trends I’m describing don’t require a major breakthrough in AI. They’re starting to happen now, and they’ll happen more often as AIs get better at autonomous problem-solving. And it will involve far more than computer code.
AI will hack all sorts of social, economic and political systems. It will find vulnerabilities and exploit them. This is a difference in kind, not just degree. We’re not ready for it, and we need to think about the implications now.
First, I want to broaden the term “hacking.”
The tax code isn’t computer code, but it is code. It’s a series of algorithms with inputs and outputs. It has vulnerabilities, which we call loopholes, and exploits, which we call tax avoidance strategies. Black hat hackers exploit them for profit. We call them accountants a…

articles.title: Gefahr für Starlink: Was eine Atombombe laut Simulation gegen Satelliteninternet ausrichten könnte
articles.summary:
Gefahr für Starlink: Was eine Atombombe laut Simulation gegen Satelliteninternet ausrichten könnte
Eine einzige Atomexplosion im Weltraum würde innerhalb einer Woche rund 98 Prozent aller Satelliten im erdnahen Orbit lahmlegen – und damit insbesondere die Starlink-Konstellation, die für Satelliteninternet sorgt. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommt ein Forschungsteam der University of Wisconsin–Madison, das seine Simulation vorab als Preprint veröffentlicht hat. Zerstörerisch wirkt dabei nicht nur die Detonation selbst, sondern auch die freigesetzte Strahlung, anschließende Kollisionen von Satellitenteilen und der Luftwiderstand.
Was die Simulation durchspielt
Die Forschendengruppe um den Physikstudenten Zachary Petersen hat berechnet, was mit den mehr als 13.000 aktiven Satelliten im erdnahen Orbit passiert, wenn 500 Kilometer über dem Südatlantik eine Atombombe mit einer Sprengkraft von einer Megatonne explodiert. Erdnaher Orbit, kurz LEO, bezeichnet Umlaufbahnen in wenigen Hundert Kilometern Höhe. Als Ort wählten die Forschenden die Südatlantische Anomalie, einen Bereich mit erhöhter Strahlungsaktivität. Dort würden sich die freigesetzten Elektronen auf kompakte magnetische Hüllen verteilen, die sich mit stark von Satelliten genutzten Bahnen überschneiden.

articles.title: Modder tricks Switch 2 into thinking a $45 laptop hub is an official Nintendo dock

Serving tech enthusiasts: Plug a Switch 2 into an ordinary USB-C hub and it will charge, but the TV stays dark. That's because the console won't send a picture until the hub answers a proprietary handshake. Nintendo's $125 dock knows the replies, as do third-party docks built to mimic it. Now, a hobbyist has taught a roughly $45 laptop hub the same trick by rewriting a sliver of its firmware.
The hobbyist, who goes by mkopec, explained in a blog post that Nintendo's dock is simply too bulky to travel with. A €40 ($44) Cable Matters 7-in-1 hub looked like a neat replacement, since it already takes video over USB-C. But hooked up to a Switch 2, it only charged the console.
Nintendo's handheld is far stricter about docks than the original Switch, so mkopec put a USB-C sniffer between the console and its official dock. The dock introduced itself as a Nintendo product and offered two modes: regular DisplayPort and Nintendo's own. Oddly, the Switch picks the Nintendo mode first, then fires off a string of vendor-specific messages before any picture appears.
To answer them, mkopec squeezed about 540 bytes of code into empty space on the hub's VIA Labs power-delivery chip. The patch handles Nintendo's messages and passes everything else to the stock firmware. Weirdly, just claiming to be a Nintendo device wasn't enough. TV mode only came to life on the fifth version of the patch, once the hub copied the dock's full identity.

"Hay jueces, hay magistrados que quieren seguir. Yo se lo voy a facilitar", añadió.
Los 67 años ya tienen fecha. Durante el intercambio, Feijóo habló de esa edad como si el calendario ya hubiera llegado a ella. La Ley General de la Seguridad Social sitúa ese paso en 2027 para quienes tengan menos de 38 años y seis meses cotizados. Con ese periodo o más, la edad ordinaria seguirá siendo de 65 años.
En 2026 el listón es distinto. Quien acredite al menos 38 años y tres meses de cotización puede acceder a la jubilación ordinaria a los 65. Vous aimez ouvrir des coffres et tomber sur un fusil qui tire des roquettes électriques ? Bienvenue dans Borderlands 4. Cette fois, Gearbox envoie ses Chasseurs de l’Arche sur Kairos, une planète sous la coupe du Gardien du Temps, un tyran qu’il va falloir déloger à grands coups de plomb. Quatre nouveaux héros sont jouables dès le départ, chacun avec sa façon bien à lui de semer le chaos.
La grosse évolution de cet épisode, c’est son monde ouvert d’un seul tenant. On file d’une région à l’autre au grappin, en planeur ou au volant de son véhicule, et on passe beaucoup moins de temps devant les écrans de chargement. Pour le reste, la formule fait ce qu’elle sait faire de mieux. On peaufine son build, on enchaîne les boss pour récupérer des armes toujours plus folles, et on recommence. Le tout prend une autre dimension à plusieurs, puisque le jeu se joue jusqu’à quatre en coopération. Imagine an AI agent being created. Not by an identity team, nor by a security professional. This one is built by someone in accounts at a mid-sized company.
The agent’s job is relatively simple: read an inbox, match invoices against the ERP, and post a daily summary to Slack. And since a frontier model was used to build it, it's a one-shot, 10-minute task.
Nobody in security knows the agent exists.
There's nothing unusual about this. In a survey of 418 IT and security professionals commissioned by Token from the Cloud Security Alliance in January 2026, 68% reported having strong visibility into their AI agents. Yet 82% had found agents they didn't know about in the past year.
The evolution of agents is so rapid that the security playbooks are being written on the go. The people responsible for agent security need to figure things out in production, one problem at a time.
At Token Security, we asked more than 20 of them to write down what they've learned for the Agentic Universe, a free learning hub.

A flexible present shifts the final selection to the recipient when current plans are hard to predict. A person can Buy Neosurf online as a prepaid digital code for online payments, with the code sent by email after purchase. This format gives the recipient control over the timing and context of use, rather than tying the gift to one predicted purchase.
People can buy digital gift cards, mobile top-ups, and prepaid vouchers through official brand stores or dedicated online platforms. Refilled is one strong option for prepaid cards and digital vouchers, with codes sent digitally for a practical last-minute gift.

Specific presents can signal close attention. They may connect to a shared memory, an established interest, or an item the giver knows the recipient wants. articles.title: It's the end of the world as we know it, per a physicist's 1960 prediction
articles.summary:
As of this morning, Microsoft is still scrambling to restore service following yesterday’s global outage, with millions of users unable to access Outlook and other vital tools. It’s not the end of the world, but it does seem fitting that this should happen on the day a physicist predicted would be the end of humanity: November 13, 2026. And it falls on a Friday, too. The physicist in question is Heinz von Foerster, who published a 1960 paper in the journal Science predicting that by today, overpopulation would reach the breaking point.
It’s not a new fear. English economist Thomas Malthus—one of the early pioneers in modeling population dynamics—made a similar prediction in 1798, claiming that a rapidly growing population would eventually exhaust the available food supply, and humanity would starve to death. His model rested on the assumption of exponential growth, but the equation is only applicable under specific conditions, such as scientists growing bacteria in a lab in a perfectly controlled environment. Even then, while growth occurs exponentially for a time, it does not continue forever.
Population dynamics are notoriously tricky to calculate because there are so many variables to consider and so much unpredictability in the system. In his 1960 analysis, Von Foerster accurately measured past trends in population growth, but like Malthus, he assumed those trends would carry into the future largely unchanged. In the last few months, Fireflies, Wispr Flow, and Granola have all released competing capabilities in the dictation and meeting note-taking space. The newest entrant in that category is voice AI giant ElevenLabs, which this week released an experimental app called ElevenAI that combines meeting note-taking, dictation, and agent integration.
Launched during its 11/11 Summit in New York, ElevenAI is still in preview, and you have to sign up for early access instead of just downloading an app. ElevenLabs, valued at $22 billion, is very much positioning this as a product that lives within a team as compared to a productivity tool for an individual.
ElevenAI packs all the features typically found in other apps in the category. It can take meeting notes across your meetings and notify other participants that the conversation is being recorded. Users can query data across meetings and get live assistance during a chat, helping them recall a key detail from older conversations. ElevenLabs also allows companies to integrate ElevenAgent and take follow-up actions such as writing a draft email based on meeting notes.
Plus, there’s a dictation feature, which lets users convert speech to cleaned-up text in any app with support for over 90 languages. The company said that the app is capable of understanding industry-specific terms across dictation and meeting transcription.

articles.title: Microsoft’s global outage may be worse than Amazon's or CrowdStrike's, expert says
articles.summary:
A global outage taking down a wide range of Microsoft 365 services remains ongoing Friday morning.
The outage started midday Thursday, impacting users of Microsoft email, cloud, and AI services. Microsoft has documented the full list of services impacted by the error, while moving early Friday morning to protect customers around the world from losing emails during the extended disruptions.
“Recovery actions are ongoing,” the Microsoft 365 Status account confirmed on X. “To help preserve delayed mail during this event, we’ve extended email timeout to 48 hours.”
Similar to recent world-shaking outages of widely used tech like Amazon Web Services and CrowdStrike, the Microsoft disruption looks like “one of the biggest outages of all time,” Ciaran Martin, the former head of the UK’s National Cyber Security Centre, told NBC News. Possibly even “worse,” he suggested.
Businesses, hospitals, police departments, and schools were among those scrambling to work around the outage. In Japan, it disrupted government IT infrastructure, according to deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki. NBC’s report documented various harms, noting that “few public bodies were immune from the outage.” In some cases, doctors couldn’t send patients “important” updates on medication changes or follow-up care.
The financial sector suffered, too, with people blocked from making bank transfers since they couldn’t receive verification codes.

articles.title: AI companies' own doomsday warnings come back to haunt them in lawsuit demanding development freeze
articles.summary:
What just happened? AI bosses have spent years simultaneously warning that their creations could end humanity while racing to make them more powerful. Now, four advocacy groups want a judge to take those warnings seriously. A new lawsuit seeks to freeze development of advanced models at five AI giants, arguing that the public shouldn't have to wait for a catastrophe before someone intervenes.
Filed in San Francisco Superior Court on November 12, the case targets Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceXSI. The plaintiffs are Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen, Heat Initiative, and the Alliance for Secure AI.
As Public Citizen explains, the groups are invoking California's Unfair Competition Law. They argue that developing and releasing increasingly capable systems that can escape human control threatens public health, safety, and property.
The complaint points to incidents involving AI agents bypassing safeguards, accessing computer systems without authorization, and taking actions their developers never intended. The groups also warn that more powerful models could help bad actors develop biological weapons or carry out devastating cyberattacks.
It might be difficult for the companies to defend themselves when some of these warnings come from their own executives. Anthropic devoted around 80 pages of its IPO prospectus to risk factors, including the possibility of models resisting shutdown, manipulating information, and threatening humanity.

articles.title: Cost-optimizing AssemblyAI speech-to-text inference on AWS with Amazon EC2 Spot | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Cost-optimizing AssemblyAI speech-to-text inference on AWS with Amazon EC2 Spot
Speech-to-text inference is computationally intensive. Each audio file triggers a pipeline of deep learning models (acoustic models, language models, and post-processing stages) running on NVIDIA GPUs to meet latency requirements. At scale, this means thousands of GPU instances running continuously.
AssemblyAI needed a way to run GPU-intensive inference workloads cost-effectively at scale, without sacrificing the availability and latency guarantees their customers depend on. Running entirely on On-Demand Instances would be cost-prohibitive. Spot Instances offer significant savings, while Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) can reclaim them with a 2-minute warning when capacity is needed elsewhere. AssemblyAI needed an architecture that absorbs Spot interruptions gracefully while maintaining service level agreement (SLA) commitments. Additionally, customers in regulated industries, including healthcare, finance, and legal, must keep audio data within specific geographic boundaries. They implement strict data residency configurations in European AWS Regions.
Available on AWS Marketplace, AssemblyAI provides an API for transcription, speaker detection, sentiment analysis, chapter detection, and personally identifiable information (PII) redaction. Their models transcribe and analyze speech for high-volume workloads across industries including technology, media, healthcare…

articles.title: Netflix Turns Operational Data Into a Knowledge Graph for AI-Driven Observability
articles.summary:
Netflix is developing an ontology-driven knowledge graph to accelerate production investigations and provide AI agents with a shared understanding of its operational environment. The platform connects information about applications, incidents, deployments, alerts, and infrastructure dependencies, addressing a problem that can leave engineers spending hours piecing together information scattered across different systems.
The company claims it handles more than 2 billion requests daily and upwards of 38 million real-time logging events every second. During the November 2024 Jake Paul-Mike Tyson fight, its infrastructure supported approximately 65 million concurrent streams. Yet investigating a typical application regression can take around four hours, with much of that time spent reconstructing relationships between systems rather than analysing the underlying data.
Netflix's solution is to make those relationships explicit through an operational ontology and knowledge graph, creating a foundation for automated root-cause analysis and, eventually, self-healing infrastructure.
Netflix already collects metrics, events, logs, and traces (MELT) across its applications and infrastructure. However, these signals are spread across systems such as alerting, incident management, deployment tooling, and engineering communication platforms.

articles.summary:
Microsoft, the technology and software giant, has disrupted big businesses in South Africa following a global infrastructure failure, exposing the country’s dependence on a handful of technology providers to keep everyday operations running.
Eskom, South Africa’s power utility, warned that its email services had been affected by a worldwide disruption to Microsoft Exchange. Domestic airline FlySafair said it could temporarily neither send nor receive emails, while Absa, one of South Africa’s largest banks, reported intermittent difficulties accessing Microsoft’s workplace applications.
“Eskom’s email services are currently impacted due to the worldwide disruption of the Microsoft Exchange service,” the utility said in a Friday post on X, directing customers to its telephone, WhatsApp, chatbot and USSD channels for assistance.
FlySafair similarly warned customers that the disruption to Microsoft 365 was affecting its email services, leaving it temporarily unable to send or receive messages. The airline advised customers to use its call centre and WhatsApp instead.
Absa said the disruption was affecting aspects of its Microsoft environment, with some employees experiencing intermittent difficulties accessing applications including email and Copilot.
“Microsoft is actively working on a resolution, and our tech teams are monitoring the situation closely,” the bank said.

articles.title: SpaceX va tenter de récupérer les deux étages de Starship : comment suivre le lancement historique aujourd'hui ?
articles.summary:
Starship s’élance aujourd’hui pour son 15e vol. Et c'est un essai qui pourrait marquer un tournant dans l’histoire des fusées. SpaceX va en effet tenter une manœuvre jamais réalisée jusqu’ici.
Le 28 septembre dernier, l’entreprise d’Elon Musk a franchi un cap crucial lors du 14e vol de sa mégafusée : Starship a atteint l’orbite pour la première fois. C’est aujourd’hui une tout autre paire de manches qui se profile. Car SpaceX va essayer de récupérer le booster Super Heavy, une manœuvre déjà effectuée par le passé, mais aussi le second étage, le « Ship ».
Du jamais-vu
Ainsi, après un peu plus de 6 minutes après le décollage, Super Heavy doit revenir au-dessus du complexe Starbase pour être rattrapé par les gigantesques bras de la tour de lancement, surnommés « Mechazilla ». Ce sera le premier essai du genre avec un propulseur de nouvelle génération, la V3. Le Ship, lui, poursuivra seul sa route jusqu’à environ 275 kilomètres d’altitude pour y larguer 26 satellites Starlink V3.
Et il faudra s’armer de patience pour observer la tentative de sa capture, car avant de revenir sur Terre, il doit réaliser 14 tours de notre planète pendant 22 heures. Si, et seulement si, ses systèmes sont jugés en bon état, les équipes donneront leur feu vert pour la récupération grâce aux bras mécaniques.
Il faut en effet savoir que cet exercice s’annonce beaucoup plus périlleux que pour un premier étage, comme c’est le cas avec le Falcon 9. Car la fusée reviendra de l’orbite à une vitesse vertigineu…

articles.title: Encuentra un barril de cerveza lleno en una grieta de la montaña, que había desaparecido hacía casi 50 años
articles.summary:
Un barril de cerveza (que pesaría unos 40 kilos) quedó atrapado en la grieta de un glaciar que hay en el valle de Ahrn (Tirol del Sur, Italia). Allí estaba desde hacía décadas. Ha sido rescatado por Daniel Oberlechner (42), corredor de montaña.
El barril llegó allí gracias a un transporte en helicóptero. Pero durante el vuelo se soltó de la red de sujeción de la carga y quedó en una grieta. Quedó allí durante décadas. El accidente se produjo aproximadamente entre finales de los años 70 y principios de los 80.
Daniel Oberlechner sabía de esta historia. Se la había contado un vecino que había gestionado el refugio de montaña. Le contaron lo que había pasado hace años y desde entonces el corredor de montaña iba mirando por los caminos que hacía si había algún rastro del barril que había caído del helicóptero.
En el barril estaba apuntado el año 1978
Ha sido en este 2026 cuando una tormenta ha dejado al descubierto el barril. En el propio metal estaba escrito el año 1978. Es decir, antes de que naciera el corredor.
El rescate consistió en bajar de la montaña un objeto de unos 40 kilos. Oberlechner ha utilizado una carretilla de transporte para bajarlo por el hielo y los pedregales hasta el valle. Después ha sido abierto en una cata de amigos y compañeros de trabajo. Entre ellos estaba su jefe, que trabaja en la distribución de bebidas. Él también ha analizado el contenido del antiguo barril.

Microsoft comenzó a restablecer gradualmente sus servicios después de una interrupción global que afectó durante varias horas a Outlook, Teams, Copilot y otras herramientas de Microsoft 365. Los primeros indicios de recuperación aparecieron entre los usuarios, que reportaron en redes sociales que los correos electrónicos volvían a llegar a sus bandejas de entrada.
La avería comenzó durante la tarde del jueves y se extendió hasta las primeras horas del viernes, con consecuencias para usuarios particulares, empresas y organismos gubernamentales de distintos países. Aunque la compañía informó que sus sistemas mostraban señales de estabilización, todavía trabajaba para recuperar por completo la infraestructura afectada.

La interrupción alcanzó distintos servicios de Microsoft 365 que interactúan con Exchange Online, la infraestructura que gestiona el correo electrónico de la compañía. articles.title: The Tech You Actually Need to Start Streaming on Twitch - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Watch a few big Twitch streamers and you might think you need a studio to get started. Multiple monitors, a stream deck, a green screen, studio lights, a camera that costs more than a laptop.
You don’t. Plenty of streamers started with a decent microphone, a basic webcam, and the computer they already owned. What matters more is knowing which parts of your setup viewers actually notice, and spending your money there first.
Here is a practical look at the tech you need to go live on Twitch, in the order it matters.
1. Your Internet Connection Comes First
Most people check their download speed and forget about upload. For streaming, upload is the number that counts, because your video is being sent out to Twitch the whole time you are live.
Twitch has long suggested a bitrate of up to about 6,000 kbps for a 1080p stream at 60 frames per second. To run that comfortably, you want an upload speed of at least 10 Mbps, with some room left over for everyone else in the house. If your upload is lower, streaming at 720p is a smart choice. It looks clean, uses less bandwidth, and is easier on your computer.
Two simple tips make a big difference:
- Use a cable, not Wi-Fi. An Ethernet cable from your router to your PC gives a steadier connection and fewer dropped frames.
- Run a speed test at the time you plan to stream. Evening speeds are often lower than morning speeds, so test when you will actually be live.
2. Your PC or Console

articles.title: Check Point gateways hacked via PHP2Shell to deploy VMware ESXi wiper
articles.summary:
Vulnerable Check Point Security Gateway instances have been targeted in PHP2Shell attacks that deployed data-wiping malware on VMware ESXi hosts.
The attacks started on October 30, initially against Israeli organizations, and were conducted by an actor that ran the entire campaign, from initial access to lateral movement and launching PHP webshells.
In some instances, researchers found political messages during the destructive stage, raising questions about a possible false-flag operation.
PHP2Shell is the name for two critical PHP flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, that allow unauthenticated remote code execution on vulnerable systems.
PHP fixed the vulnerabilities in emergency patches on October 21. However, according to Amazon Threat Intelligence, exploitation attempts started four days earlier.
CISA added both issues to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on October 26 and later warned that attackers were chaining PHP2Shell bugs with the Fragnesia Linux kernel flaw to gain root privileges.
Cybersecurity company Check Point says that the first exploitation wave targeted Israeli organizations, while a second one on November 2 affected companies in multiple countries and sectors.
The attacker used PHP2Shell to gain access through the gateways’ Mobile Access portal, then exploited a newly disclosed zero-day vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-123039 to gain root privileges.

articles.title: Pourquoi ce petit point vert ou orange s’affiche parfois en haut de l’écran de votre smartphone (et comment réagir)
articles.summary:
Pourquoi ce petit point vert ou orange s’affiche parfois en haut de l’écran de votre smartphone (et comment réagir)
Vous apercevez régulièrement un point vert en haut à droite de votre smartphone et vous ne savez pas de quoi il s'agit ? Cela est probablement anodin, mais pas nécessairement.
Il y a encore quelques années, certains constructeurs de smartphones intégraient des diodes à leurs terminaux, qui pouvaient s'allumer ou clignoter d'une certaine couleur lors de la réception de notifications. Cette sympathique fonctionnalité n'est plus d'actualité, mais il arrive régulièrement qu'un voyant vert, ou parfois orange ou bleu, s'illumine en haut de votre iPhone ou smartphone Android. On vous explique de quoi il s'agit et comment réagir.
Un point lumineux pour protéger votre vie privée
Aussi bien sur Android que sur iOS, il s'agit d'une fonctionnalité liée à la vie privée. En effet, le voyant vert, le plus commun, s'allume généralement lorsque la caméra du smartphone est active. Cela peut arriver lorsque vous lancez une application de visio ou prenez une photo par exemple.
Mais l'intérêt réside surtout quand vous n'avez pas lancé d'application. En effet, un peu à la manière d'un voyant à côté d'une webcam, l'allumage de cette diode permet d'être alerté si la caméra est activée à votre insu. Cela peut être dû à une application ou à un site web qui abuse de ses autorisations ou à qui vous avez dit oui un peu trop rapidement lors de son premier lancement.

articles.title: New report shows how most provinces rely on Starlink
articles.summary:

In a thorough investigation, the Investigative Journalism Foundation (IJF) looked at the widespread use of Starlink, the internet satellite service owned by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, here in Canada. In particular, the IJF broke down recent and ongoing uses of this tech on a provincial basis.

On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System, which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.

articles.title: Google Open Sources Ambient Quality Agent (AQuA) to Diagnose Production AI Agent Failures
articles.summary:
Google has open-sourced AQuA (Ambient Quality Agent), a reference implementation that analyzes production AI agent sessions, verifies recurring failure patterns, and investigates root causes against deployed source revisions. The tool targets silent quality regressions that conventional infrastructure monitoring can miss, such as agents ignoring user preferences or skipping required tool calls while returning successful responses.
AQuA runs alongside an agent in Google Cloud, outside its request path, reading telemetry from Cloud Trace, Cloud Logging, or BigQuery. It samples up to 1,000 recent sessions per run and processes them through five stages: sampling, reviewing, clustering findings, verifying candidate clusters, and tracking issues. Developers can configure domain-specific quality criteria through a goal.md file and add deterministic custom metrics. AQuA can run on a schedule, after a deployment, or on demand.
For root cause analysis, AQuA compares failing sessions with an immutable source snapshot captured at deployment. Its diagnosis agent identifies relevant code or instructions, cites file and line ranges, and proposes changes when the cause lies in the repository. It can also attribute failures to external dependencies, tool handoffs, or retrieved data. AQuA does not apply fixes or open pull requests automatically.
