articles.title: Architecture patterns for fast session startup on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Architecture patterns for fast session startup on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime
Agents today review code, process claims, and run unattended for hours. Many also sit behind interactive experiences where a person waits for the first response. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime gives these agents a fully managed, serverless environment: each session runs in its own isolated microVM, the platform scales to zero when there’s no work, and you only pay for the resources your sessions consume.
AgentCore runtime with platformVersion set to “V2” changes how sessions start. Instead of initializing your container for every session, it prepares your environment once, snapshots it, and restores that snapshot for each new session. Session start times are faster and more consistent. V2 also reclaims memory your sessions don’t use, so your bill tracks what your agent uses.
For most agents, switching to V2 is all it takes. Some agents need restructuring to get the full benefit, and for chat and voice experiences even 2 seconds is too slow. This post explains how V2 starts a session, how to measure session start time, and how to keep work off the first request, including build hooks, which AgentCore runtime now supports. We cover four patterns, from changes to your agent’s code to starting sessions before users need them.

La norma obliga a los dueños a garantizar unas condiciones adecuadas para sus animales y a evitar situaciones peligrosas, tanto en verano como en invierno.
Qué dice la ley. El artículo 24.2.d establece la obligación de “no dejarlos solos dentro de vehículos cerrados, expuestos a condiciones térmicas o de cualquier otra índole que puedan poner su vida en peligro”. El peligro del coche al sol. Pero el riesgo más evidente es cómo sube la temperatura dentro de un vehículo aparcado, sobre todo si se queda al sol, y bajar un poco las ventanillas apenas cambia las cosas, tal y como explica la Asociación Americana de Medicina Veterinaria (AVMA). Y con el calor en general, el Colegio de Veterinarios de León advierte del riesgo de golpes de calor y de deshidratación en perros y gatos expuestos al so.

    Pour aller plus loin
AMD installerait de la mémoire GDDR7 dédiée sur ses futurs APUs Zen 6 / RDNA 5
            
D’après de nouvelles indiscrétions, l’architecture baptisée Siren Halo embarquerait de la mémoire vidéo GDDR7 dédiée, exactement celle qui équipe les cartes GeForce RTX 50, en complément de la mémoire système classique. On reviendrait ainsi au schéma traditionnel d’un PC portable de joueur, à ceci près que l’ensemble logerait sur un seul et même support.

articles.title: The Future of Video Editing: Can AI Tools Replace Traditional Editing Software? - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Video editing used to demand expensive hardware, years of practice, and a lot of patience. Today, you can describe a scene in a sentence and watch software assemble it in minutes.
Auto-captions, background removal, script-to-video generators, and one-click highlight reels are now ordinary features, which raises a question every creator, marketer, and filmmaker is asking: will AI replace traditional editing software?
The short answer is no, at least not entirely. The longer answer is more interesting, because AI is changing what “editing” means, who can do it, and which skills matter most.
How We Got Here
Traditional editing software like Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, and DaVinci Resolve is built around a timeline, with clips, layers, keyframes, and effects arranged by hand. This gives editors precise control, but it also creates a steep learning curve. Mastering color grading, audio mixing, and motion graphics can take years.
AI tools approach the problem differently. Instead of asking you to manipulate every frame, they ask what you want to achieve. You provide a script, a few clips, or a text prompt, and the system handles cutting, pacing, captioning, and sometimes even generating the footage itself. A ChatGPT video generator and editor is a good example of this shift: it lets you work through conversation and prompts rather than menus and timelines.

Artificial Intelligence
Route coding agent requests to the right model on Amazon Bedrock with NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard
Coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex CLI work in tasks. A developer asks for a change, and the agent reads files, edits code, and runs tests until the work is done. One task can take a few model calls or dozens. What the developer pays for is the task, not one call.
The price per token alone doesn’t tell you what a whole task costs. The total depends on how many turns a model needs, how much history each turn replays, and how often a task has to be retried or never finishes. You pay for every attempt, including attempts on tasks that never finish. So when you route a coding agent’s requests between models, judge the routing by cost per solved task: the total cost of your runs divided by the number of runs whose tests pass.
NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard is an open source library that helps an AI agent choose which model handles each request. You define the models that it can use and the strategy that it follows. Its LiteLLM integration supports two strategies. Stage routing reads the recent tool activity and results in the request history, and then picks one of two candidate models. Random routing picks from the configured models, with optional weights, for traffic splits and A/B comparisons. Another option you can explore is LiteLLM, who also recently shipped a native built-in Switchyard stage router as an auto-router strategy.

articles.title: Open Source DocumentDB 1.0 Reaches General Availability
articles.summary:
DocumentDB 1.0 is the first generally available release of the open source, MIT-licensed document database built on PostgreSQL, with compatibility for the MongoDB wire protocol. Most MongoDB drivers, tools, and queries work without changes.
DocumentDB consists of a PostgreSQL extension that provides MongoDB API-compatible functionality and a gateway that translates MongoDB protocol requests into PostgreSQL calls. Version 1.0 supports PostgreSQL 15–18 through container images, with Linux packages available for PostgreSQL 17 and 18, and includes a Kubernetes operator, with the GA focusing on security, stability, and fixes for indexing, aggregation, and geospatial queries.
Microsoft announced the open source project early in 2025, aiming to provide the developer community with a NoSQL datastore built on PostgreSQL, and offering full visibility into the engine's architecture and implementation. The project joined the Linux Foundation a few months later, with support from other large database organizations including AWS, Cockroach Labs, Google, Snowflake, and Yugabyte. In the recent article "DocumentDB and the MIT License: What to Know Before You Build, Deploy, and Distribute," the team explains how DocumentDB’s permissive MIT license allows commercial use, modification, and hosting without requiring disclosure of proprietary code, contrasting it with MongoDB’s SSPL.

43 milímetros. Es la mayor altura registrada en el género (todavía no se ha concretado la especie). La cúspide es ancha, curvada y de bordes doblemente aserrados. articles.title: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits
articles.summary:
Elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time.
Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured.
Accidental savanna
Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country’s four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006).
The reservoir had brought farming and settlers, some of whom lived inside what later became the park. When they were moved out, the land they had cleared for their crops turned into grassland that, according to de Silva, looks very much like an African savanna. LangChain began in 2022 as a popular open source project that handled the kinds of tasks that early-stage LLMs found difficult, like searching the web, calling APIs, and interacting with databases. As the frontier AI labs delivered harnesses that now competently do those tasks, LangChain turned its focus toward managing AI agents. It has apparently found its stride in this highly competitive area with a simple message: letting businesses own their own intelligence.
With its open source roots, the startup says its agent creation and management software, LangSmith, is not trying to lock users into any particular model, cloud, or ecosystem, unlike the major clouds or frontier AI labs. It also promises that LangSmith will contain agent behavior and is easy to use.
True, there are plenty of other startups pitching similar advantages these days and also doing well (case in point is newcomer Mintive). To digitize Blu-rays to a NAS for Plex streaming, use hardware-accelerated software like AnyMP4 Blu-ray Ripper to bypass AACS encryption and compress 40GB discs into 4GB HEVC (H.265) files with pristine 5.1 audio. For 1:1 uncompressed raw backups, MakeMKV is the standard, though it requires massive storage or secondary compression via HandBrake.
Physical Blu-ray discs are built-in bottlenecks for modern home theaters. If you want to watch a movie in another room, you have to hunt down the plastic case, hope it hasn’t suffered from disc rot, and shove it into a noisy standalone player. Moving your entire physical library to a central NAS (Network Attached Storage) running Plex or Jellyfin gives you instant, multi-room access without sacrificing the high-bitrate playback you paid for.
Key Takeaways
- The Physical Media Bottleneck: Optical drives are vanishing, and physical discs are vulnerable to scratch degradation and disc rot, locking your high-bitrate media to a single room.
- The Storage vs. Quality Dilemma: Raw 1:1 extraction (MakeMKV) preserves exact disc data but demands 35GB-40GB of NAS storage per movie, quickly overwhelming standard 4TB drives.

articles.title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
articles.summary:
GLP-1 medications are everywhere these days. The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy.
In a study published this week, researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That’s around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC’s Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report.
Among GLP-1 users, nearly half (44 percent) reported using their GLP-1 in a way that was different from how it was prescribed. Users skipped doses, delayed getting refills, and used smaller doses than prescribed, among other changes. More than half of the people modifying how they used the drug said the changes were because of cost or availability reasons. Cost and access barriers were most pronounced among younger GLP-1 users. La NASA pidió a empresas privadas propuestas para subir de órbita el telescopio espacial Hubble, que sin intervención volvería a entrar en la atmósfera terrestre en 2033 o 2034. La agencia espacial de Estados Unidos publicó la solicitud el 29 de octubre y recibirá respuestas hasta el 30 de noviembre.
La convocatoria admite tres tipos de propuestas: una misión para elevar el telescopio a mayor altura, un servicio que mejore sus capacidades o una reentrada controlada, con el fin de evitar que caiga sin control. Quien participe deberá aportar el cohete, la nave y, si corresponde, la tripulación.
La NASA calcula que cualquier misión debería realizarse antes de 2032. La agencia no tiene fondos asignados para contratar un rescate y aclaró que no se compromete a comprarlo, según informó Ars Technica a partir del texto de la solicitud.
Un telescopio sin motor que baja cada año
El Hubble orbita la Tierra desde hace más de tres décadas y no tiene sistema de propulsión propio. Como todo satélite de órbita baja, pierde altura por el roce con las capas altas de la atmósfera. Según Ars Technica, tardó 24 años en bajar de 583 kilómetros, su altitud en 2002, a unos 470 kilómetros actuales.
La solicitud pide llevarlo a por lo menos 600 kilómetros. Ese ascenso lo mantendría en órbita al menos 25 años más, según Ars Technica. New Scientist informó que la NASA estima una probabilidad de 10% de reentrada hacia septiembre de 2032 y de 50% hacia diciembre de 2033.

articles.title: Choisir une offre d'électricité ou de gaz : tout ce qu'il faut savoir avant de signer
articles.summary:
Derrière un vocabulaire très technique, les critères qui comptent vraiment pour choisir son offre d’énergie sont assez simples. Il faut regarder ce que vous consommez, quand vous le consommez, les équipements présents dans votre logement et la façon dont le prix de l’offre est construit.
L’objectif de ce guide est simple : comprendre rapidement les termes techniques, identifier les critères importants pour son logement et savoir quoi regarder avant de choisir une offre d’électricité ou de gaz.
L’essentiel pour bien choisir son offre d’énergie
- Comparez le prix de l’abonnement et celui du kWh : le premier correspond à la partie fixe de la facture, le second dépend de votre consommation.
- En électricité, adaptez la puissance souscrite à votre logement : une puissance trop faible peut provoquer des coupures, une puissance trop élevée augmente inutilement la partie fixe de la facture.
- Regardez quand vous consommez : une offre avec heures creuses ou tarification différenciée n’est intéressante que si vous pouvez réellement déplacer une partie de votre consommation.
- Pour le gaz, regardez vos usages : cuisson seule, eau chaude ou chauffage n’entraînent pas du tout le même niveau de consommation.
- Préparez votre PDL ou PRM pour l’électricité et votre PCE pour le gaz : ces identifiants permettent de retrouver précisément votre logement lors d’une souscription.
- Regardez les services associés à l’offre : qualité du service client, suivi de consommation ou possibilité de regroup…

The alert stated that all departing flights must remain on the ground “until further notice.” Inbound international flights will be “managed on a case-by-case basis,” it said.

“Today’s nationwide ground stop happened because our air traffic control system is operating on DECADES-OLD analog equipment that simply cannot compete with the demands of the 21st century,” Duffy posted on X.
Over a million travelers have been affected by the delays, with some airlines cancelling flights for the remainder of Friday. “Due to the ongoing ground stop, Air Canada has cancelled all flights to and from the United States for the remainder of the evening,” the airline said.
The stoppage began at 3:36 pm EST Friday afternoon, days after expanding use of an AI tool, when the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop, halting departures from all US airports. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy announced the ground stop on X, citing a “communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.” Duffy promised updates as more information is known and said FAA staff was troubleshooting the problem.

Der Vorteil: Das mühsame Eintippen der Kartennummer direkt beim Händler entfällt. Stattdessen wird der Bezahlvorgang „in der bekannten und sicheren Umgebung der Sparkassen-Finanzgruppe“ durchgeführt, heißt es in einer Pressemitteilung. Das bringt auch ein Plus an Sicherheit mit sich, da der Händler die Kartendetails nicht direkt mitgeteilt bekommt, sondern nur einen Token erhält.
Laut Inside Digital werden Kund:innen kein festes Passwort für den Bezahlservice vergeben. Zahlungen sollen sich stattdessen per Einmalcode, der an die hinterlegte E-Mail-Adresse verschickt wird, oder über die S-pushTAN-App bestätigen lassen.

articles.title: Por qué fallaron los servicios de Outlook, Teams, OneDrive, Copilot y SharePoint en el mundo
articles.summary:
La interrupción mundial de Microsoft 365 dejó sin acceso o con fallas intermitentes a usuarios de Outlook, Microsoft Teams, OneDrive, Copilot y SharePoint. El incidente, que comenzó el jueves 12 de noviembre, se originó en problemas de conexión de servidores de Exchange Online, la plataforma que administra el correo, los calendarios y los contactos de las cuentas corporativas.
Microsoft descartó en sus primeras actualizaciones que el problema respondiera a un aumento extraordinario de usuarios o a un ciberataque. Su explicación apuntó a una pérdida inesperada de servidores, que redujo la capacidad disponible y trasladó más tráfico a los equipos que continuaban en funcionamiento.

articles.title: Generative AI Video Tools: How AI Video Extenders Work - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Every creator knows the feeling: a clip that is almost right, but ends two seconds too soon. The product reveal cuts off before the viewer sees the whole thing; the landscape shot stops just as the camera reaches the best angle. Until recently, the only fixes were to reshoot, slow the footage down until it looked soft, or cut around the gap and hope nobody noticed.
Generative AI has added a fourth option: AI video extenders look at the end of a clip and create new footage that continues it — the same subject, movement, and light, carried forward for a few more seconds. The result is newly generated video, not a loop or a frozen frame — built to pick up exactly where the original left off.
Image source: Unsplash — photo by Nejc Soklic
What Is an AI Video Extender?
An AI video extender lengthens an existing video by generating additional frames beyond its current ending. You give it a short clip, and sometimes a short text instruction describing what should happen next. The tool studies the final frames — the subject’s position, its direction of movement, the camera’s motion, the background — and renders new frames that continue the action.
The idea sits inside the wider family of generative AI video tools, alongside text-to-video generators and image-to-video animators. What makes an extender different is its starting point: it does not invent a scene from nothing, it inherits one. That constraint is also its strength — the generated seconds have a real reference to match, whi…

articles.title: Offshore VPS Explained: When Australians Should Host Outside the Country - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
A Melbourne SaaS company with 70% of its customers in Europe pays for a Sydney server, and every user in Berlin or London pays for it too, in milliseconds that pile up on each click.
The fix sounds obvious (move the application closer to the people using it), yet the word “offshore” makes plenty of owners hesitate, as if a rack in Frankfurt were shadier than one in Sydney. So where should an Australian business actually host?
What Offshore VPS Really Means
For anyone asking what is offshore vps, it is simply a virtual private server hosted outside the country where a business operates. It works like a regular VPS, with allocated CPU, RAM and storage, but gives businesses more flexibility in choosing where their websites and applications run. This can mean better access for international customers, different pricing options or hosting arrangements that better suit their needs.
Keep in mind that the server’s physical location, the provider’s registered country and the laws governing stored data may differ, so always check where the infrastructure is based and which terms apply.
When Does Moving Abroad Pay Off?
An Australian business with most of its customers in Europe may find that hosting its website closer to them makes more sense than keeping everything on a server in Sydney. Shorter network routes can reduce latency and improve response times, particularly for applications that exchange data frequently. articles.title: The banking app is becoming part of the checkout experience - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Banking apps are no longer just for checking balances and transferring money. Today, online banking plays an increasingly important role in digital shopping.
Account-to-account (A2A) payments make this possible. They connect banking apps and online checkouts, letting customers pay directly from their accounts.
This changes the user experience, making digital transactions effortless. But what does this mean for online businesses?
What makes bank-based checkout possible?
Behind bank-based checkout is a simple principle: money moves between bank accounts without passing through card networks. This is known as account-to-account (A2A) payments.
However, not all A2A payments work the same way. Some use open banking, which allows authorised third-party providers to initiate payments from customers’ bank accounts with their consent. Instead of entering card details, customers can authorise payments through their banking app or online banking.
Other A2A payments rely on local banking networks or real-time payment systems. For example, India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) lets customers pay directly from their bank accounts through a domestic infrastructure.
Regardless of what powers different A2A solutions, the key principle remains the same: the money is transferred from the customer’s bank account directly to the merchant’s. In some cases, it happens in real time.

AI privacy starts with your data
Protecting data privacy as AI gains greater access and autonomy
As businesses give AI applications and agents access to more internal systems, data privacy is becoming harder to manage. Much of the focus has been on the risk of AI models surfacing sensitive or confidential information in their responses. But the privacy challenge starts earlier. Organizations also need to understand what data AI systems can access in the first place, where that data comes from and how it is being used.
Technical Product Marketing Director at Qlik.
That challenge is already holding AI adoption back. 95% of enterprises have delayed or cancelled AI projects because of infrastructure and data governance challenges. As AI gains greater autonomy and access to company data, businesses need to get the foundations right before privacy risks become impossible to contain.
Before information reaches the model
Data privacy is not just a legal or compliance concern. It should matter to everyone who touches data within an organization. With AI, the consequences of getting it wrong are growing, from exposing sensitive information to damaging customer trust and brand reputation.
These risks can emerge before sensitive data ever reaches an AI model. Poorly classified, duplicated or outdated data can carry existing privacy problems into AI applications, turning weaknesses previously contained within individual systems into much wider risks.

A frustração com respostas erradas e instruções ignoradas está por trás de boa parte dos xingamentos enviados a chatbots de inteligência artificial. Entre as mensagens ofensivas, 19% apareceram depois que a ferramenta deixou de seguir uma instrução. En effet, la relation extraconjugale de Jensen Huang, ex-dirigeant de Nvidia, avec Alice Huang, suspectée d’être une espionne au service de la Chine, pourrait aboutir à un durcissement supplémentaire des restrictions américaines sur les exportations de puces Nvidia vers la Chine.

articles.title: El USB del espacio: Europa crea un conector universal para reparar satélites en órbita en lugar de tirarlos

¿Te imaginas que tu móvil se queda sin batería o te da el más mínimo fallo, lo tiras a la basura y te compras otro? Básicamente eso es lo que se hace con los satélites en el espacio. Cuando se quedan sin combustible o sufren algún daño, generalmente se abandonan y se sustituyen, de modo que el viejo pasa a engrosar las filas de la basura espacial. Lo ideal sería enviar naves capaces de transmitir energía, datos, calor y otros recursos necesarios para reparar los satélites, de modo que puedan seguir usándose. Sin embargo, eso requiere el uso de conectores compatibles tanto con el satélite como con la nave de reparación.
Ante este problema, un equipo de investigadores europeos ha desarrollado un conector universal que valdría para la tecnología de distintos tipos de satélite. Se llama Space USB y de momento solo se ha probado en laboratorio, pero con muy buenos resultados.
Dos años de desarrollo. El proyecto Space USB se puso en marcha el 1 de enero de 2024 y finalizó el 31 de diciembre de 2025, gracias al trabajo de un equipo de científicos coordinado por Raphael Boissonnade, de Thales Alenia Space Francia. El objetivo, a grandes rasgos, era buscar una interfaz común a todas las tecnologías satelitales que hay en el espacio. Se bautizó como Space USB porque el principio es muy parecido al del sistema USB que se emplea en tecnologías informáticas terrestres. articles.title: Microsoft Turns On Memory Integrity for More Windows 11 PCs With November Update
articles.summary:
Friday, November 13th 2026
Microsoft Turns On Memory Integrity for More Windows 11 PCs With November Update
Plenty of Windows 11 PCs upgraded from Windows 10 could find Memory Integrity switched on after this month's Patch Tuesday. The November security update, KB5132061, carries over a change from the optional October 28 preview (KB5127936) that lets Windows enable Memory Integrity, also called Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity (HVCI), on eligible devices during the update. Microsoft first announced the plan in September, and the change applies to Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2 as a gradual rollout. PCs where a user or IT admin already turned the feature off are left alone.
Memory Integrity depends on Virtualization-Based Security (VBS), with driver verification handled inside a hypervisor-managed environment, so malware that takes over the kernel still can't sneak in an unverified driver. Windows runs readiness checks on hardware, drivers, and performance first, and also enables VBS on PCs that lack it. It looks like eligible systems need at least an 8th Gen Intel or AMD Zen 2 processor. The performance cost hasn't gone away, though. Tom's Hardware's 2023 testing with a Core i9-13900K and RTX 4090 showed an average drop of around 5% in games, up to 10% in some titles. Microsoft told gamers in a 2022 support article, since pulled, to disable it for better performance, which is a bit awkward next to its promise to make Windows the best place to play.Some games want it on anyway, …

“Tan listo para unas cosas y tan tonto para otras”. Lo que podría ser el tópico espetado a un niño prodigio cuando se le ve fallar en operaciones tan simples como el saber relacionarse con otros niños en el patio de colegio, puede tener en el fondo parte de razón; y lo que es más, raíces biológicas heredadas de siglos y siglos de ancestros. Esto es lo que dice la ciencia sobre los inteligentes tristes y solitarios.
Mejor solo que neciamente acompañado: en 2016 dos investigadores publicaron en el British Journal of Psychology un concienzudo análisis sobre más de 15.000 sujetos y cuyos hallazgos han sido desde entonces muy compartidos: los individuos de alta inteligencia experimentan un nivel de satisfacción personal más bajo cuando socializan con amigos frecuentemente, lo que promueve la reclusión del sujeto.
La teoría de la felicidad de la sabana: los investigadores apoyaban la premisa de que los cerebros de esos sujetos superiores a la media (al menos en lo que se refiere a los campos tradicionalmente asociados con la inteligencia) se habían hecho así por la evolución y la genética. El hombre es un animal social por naturaleza, cuanta más gente tenías a tu alrededor en el pleistoceno mejor debía ser para solucionar conflictos, pero los individuos más listos, alega la psicología evolutiva, se benefician menos de ese contacto social porque son más autónomos.

articles.title: En 2004 el PSOE dio un vuelco electoral. Automáticamente los científicos notaron algo: un cambio en los embarazos y las bodas
articles.summary:
Cuando una pareja decide tener hijos valora cuestiones como su estabilidad laboral, el precio de vivienda, si tendrá o no apoyo familiar (benditos abuelos) o la marcha de la economía, pero… ¿Entra la política en esa ecuación? ¿Pueden influir unas elecciones en la demografía de un territorio, alterando, aunque sea brevemente, la natalidad, la tasa de abortos y el número de enlaces? Un estudio realizado por investigadores de la Universitat de Barcelona (UB), la Pompeu Fabra (UPF) y Cambra de Barcelona cree que sí. Y mucho.
Al menos esa es la conclusión que han sacado al analizar las elecciones de 2004, una de las más convulsas de la democracia, cuando contra todo pronóstico y pese a los sondeos que daban ganador al PP, la candidatura de José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero acabó imponiéndose con 164 escaños.
¿Demografía y elecciones? Correcto. No son dos conceptos que suelan relacionarse, pero los economistas manejan indicios (dentro y fuera de nuestro país) que sugieren que están estrechamente entrelazados. De hecho, hay pruebas de que un vuelco electoral puede tener un efecto demográfico similar al de ciertos subsidios pronatalidad, como los famosos ‘cheques bebé’ implantados en España entre 2007 y 2010.
La lógica es muy sencilla: un giro inesperado en las urnas puede levantar el ánimo y las expectativas económicas de quienes simpatizan con el partido ganador, pero hunde las de sus detractores. Y lo hace hasta tal punto que ese pesimismo acaba dejándose sentir en indicadores demográf…

Data center telemetry, sandboxed AI workloads and fleets of agents are pushing more machine-to-machine traffic through infrastructure than ever before, exposing the limits of messaging systems built for steadier demand.
That shift is drawing attention to the Neural Autonomic Transport System, an open-source messaging system that lets applications and services exchange messages by topic. Created in 2010, NATS graduated from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation in November 2026. Its simple design suits AI workloads, according to Andrew Connolly (pictured, left), NATS project maintainer at Synadia Communications Inc., a provider of managed NATS services. When AI tools like Lovable can turn a plain-language prompt into a working web app, the messaging layer has to keep updates flowing as sandboxes come and go.
“What’s changed in the current context, or landscape, is everything is really ephemeral. If you take the Lovable example, connections coming and going really fast, tons of churn, tons of sandboxes, all these things spinning up, spinning down,” Connolly said. “Not every technology can handle that.”

articles.title: Investigador publica nueva falla de Windows que da control total de la PC y aún no tiene parche
articles.summary:
Un investigador conocido como Nightmare Eclipse publicó SignDrop, una falla de Windows 11 que da control total del equipo a quien ya tenga una cuenta de usuario común. Según el portal especializado BleepingComputer, Microsoft aún no la corrigió y el autor dice que solo queda esperar su parche.
El error está en el Common Log File System (CLFS), el componente de Windows que registra eventos de programas y del sistema.
El atacante obliga a Windows Defender, el antivirus de Microsoft, a abrir un archivo de registro que él preparó. El archivo auxiliar de autenticación se crea con los permisos de Defender, y el atacante lo aprovecha para escalar a SYSTEM, el nivel más alto del sistema.
El ataque no funciona a distancia: lo puede usar alguien que ya tiene acceso local al equipo con permisos limitados, según el medio tecnológico Ars Technica. Desde ahí, según Abdelhamid Naceri, nombre real del investigador, puede apagar cualquier antivirus, porque el sistema interpreta el pedido como una acción legítima del propio programa de seguridad.
La falla nace de una defensa que la propia Microsoft introdujo en octubre de 2025 para frenar ataques contra el mismo componente. Naceri sostiene que la medida está bien implementada, pero que su lógica permite abusar de ella. El método sirve contra el sistema de autoprotección de cualquier antivirus, no solo el de Microsoft.

Voilà des années qu'on nous répète qu'IPv6 doit remplacer IPv4, mais si vous suivez un tant soit peu l'actualité réseau, vous savez qu'on n'y est toujours pas. En France, le taux d'adoption du protocole atteignait ainsi 80 % en octobre 2026, selon l'Arcep, contre environ 41 % à l'échelle mondiale, d'après l'APNIC. La transition avance, donc, mais de nombreux logiciels et services dépendent encore d'IPv4, incitant les entreprises concernées à maintenir les deux protocoles en parallèle pour éviter toute rupture de connexion. Une double gestion coûteuse, tant sur le plan financier que technique, que Microsoft entend alléger grâce à une technologie désormais disponible sur les connexions Wi-Fi et Ethernet de Windows 11 : CLAT.
IPv4 et IPv6, deux protocoles qui ne parlent pas la même langue

À l'époque, Internet était encore loin de ressembler au réseau mondial que nous connaissons, et personne n'imaginait que des dizaines de milliards d'appareils finiraient par s'y connecter.

articles.summary:
Friday, November 13th 2026
Intel's ISA Reference Confirms Razor Lake Desktop and Laptop Model IDs
Intel has added Razor Lake and Coral Rapids to the November edition of its Architecture Instruction Set Extensions Programming Reference, the document developers use to prepare software for upcoming chips. Revision 063 gives Razor Lake four new model values under family 18 (12H), the same family as Nova Lake, with 12_06H and 12_0AH covering desktop parts and 12_07H and 12_09H covering laptops. The Coral Rapids Xeon family gets 13_08H, following Diamond Rapids at 13_01H. InstLatX64 spotted the update and shared it on Bluesky.
The new feature entries are fairly small. Razor Lake picks up SSBD_PSFD_U_S, which seems to allow separate user-mode and supervisor-mode control over certain speculative memory behavior, while both families gain APIC-Timer Virtualization for virtual machines. Coral Rapids also gets a new instruction called VPMLDSABFLYDQ, aimed at ML-DSA, the quantum-resistant digital signature standard. According to Intel's GCC patches, posted this week, Razor Lake carries the same ISA feature set as Nova Lake, which should mean AVX10.2 and APX carry over, though the reference itself doesn't list Razor Lake under those rows yet. Coral Rapids sticks with AVX10.2 rather than the newer AVX10.3, at least for now.Neither family is anywhere near launch, though. articles.summary:

Modder Builds Keybytes: Modular Magnetic Keyboard System Made with Single Key Building Blocks
The world of DIY mechanical keyboards is full of niche devices with unique designs, and more than a few gimmicks. Keybytes, a new project by a modder who goes by notaroomba on GitHub via KBDnews, falls somewhere between the former and the latter, and mostly serves as an interesting proof of concept. Keybytes a modular mechanical keyboard project designed for ultimate customization. The basic idea is to have single mechanical keyboard sockets with full-height MX mechanical switches, aka Keybits, each with their own PCB and magnetic connectors that allow them to snap together, effectively creating an infinitely reconfigurable keyboard. 
The whole project hinges on the Keyword, a motherboard of sorts that contains the USB Type-C port, battery charging circuitry, and a STM32WB55 MCU. That motherboard connects to each Keybit, each of which also has its own RISC-V CH592F MCU and some clever tricks that allow the bits to connect in a rotation-agnostic way. There are also alternative PCB options, including one with a 3-axis Hall sensor, which would allow for something like a joystick or Hall effect switch implementation, and there are also spacer Keybits with power passthrough in 1u, 0.75u, and 0.5u units. A diferencia de los robots convencionales, construidos con bloques rígidos que limitan sus movimientos, estas máquinas utilizan una estructura de tensegridad: varillas duras sostenidas por una red de cables tensados que les permite plegarse, estirarse y modificar su forma según el terreno o la tarea.
El diseño, publicado en la revista científica Nature Machine Intelligence, carece de articulaciones tradicionales. Sus cuerpos tubulares tienen una garra de sujeción en cada extremo, capaces de aferrarse a otros robots o de manipular objetos.
El equipo fue dirigido por Jianguo Zhao, profesor asociado del Departamento de Ingeniería Mecánica de la CSU. El investigador definió estos sistemas como robots generalistas, con posibles aplicaciones en operaciones de búsqueda y rescate o como apoyo para trabajadores humanos en entornos de manufactura.

The reason behind this was to maintain the perception of ongoing high demand and to move an oversupply of semiconductors from TSMC. 
The WSJ report cites an August meeting between Huang and his senior finance team, including NVIDIA's CFO and acting CEO, Colette Kress, during which Kress pushed for a reduction in circular financing agreements, in response to which Huang allegedly lay into Kress, calling her a "deer in the headlights," after she had pushed to scale back NVIDIA's $250 billion deal with OpenAI. Jensen's push for further investment into small-scale cloud providers was seemingly in response to the changing tide that saw AI hyperscalers move away from off-the-shelf components in favor of custom solutions.The situation described in the report saw NVIDIA on the hook for an "avalanche" of GPUs from TSMC, for which it would have no immediate buyers. Part of the issue highlighted by Kress was also that these small-scale cloud providers NVIDIA was investing in could not afford to buy NVIDIA GPUs, meaning they, too, could be a financial dead end.

articles.title: Astro Bot Runs Natively on PC Through AnyPS5, With DLSS Frame Generation
articles.summary:
Friday, November 13th 2026
Astro Bot Runs Natively on PC Through AnyPS5, With DLSS Frame Generation
PlayStation 5 exclusive Astro Bot now runs on Windows with DLSS Super Resolution, DLSS Frame Generation, and Reflex support, thanks to an unofficial port from GitHub user imnotsharingmyname. Technically, it's a port, not running through any PS5 emulator. AnyPS5 relinks the PS5 game's x86-64 code into a Windows executable and swaps in native versions of the console's system libraries, while a GPU layer borrowed from the KytyPS5 emulator translates the graphics work to Vulkan. Players have to supply their own decrypted dump of version 01.019.000, and no game files are included.
The port hooks Astro Bot's own temporal upscale pass at runtime and feeds its color, depth, and motion vector data into DLSS through NVIDIA's Streamline SDK. On a Ryzen 5 5500, RTX 5060, and 32 GB of RAM at 1440p, the developer measured 32 to 34 FPS in Sky Garden, the heaviest area tested, and roughly 37 to 53 FPS elsewhere. Frame Generation brings that to around 63 FPS on screen, while 4x Multi Frame Generation hits 124 to 128 FPS. Apparently, the game is heavily CPU-limited, with about 22 ms of each 30 ms frame spent submitting draws on a single thread, so lowering the resolution doesn't help much. articles.title: AMD Loses Desktop CPU Share for the First Time in Months, Intel Regains Ground
articles.summary:
Friday, November 13th 2026
AMD Loses Desktop CPU Share for the First Time in Months, Intel Regains Ground
AMD's share of desktop CPU shipments fell to 29.9% in the third quarter of 2026, according to new Mercury Research data, shared by PC Gamer. That's a five-point drop from the 34.9% AMD held in Q2, with Intel climbing back to 70.1%. It's also AMD's lowest desktop figure since early 2025, when it sat at around 28%. A year ago, AMD held 33.6% of the desktop market.
Mercury itself admits it isn't sure what caused the swing. Its best guess is that weaker laptop demand let Intel shift more chips to desktops, which usually see a seasonal bump in the third quarter, after Intel had been under-supplying that market earlier in the year. AMD, on the other hand, didn't seem to get that seasonal increase. Mercury also points to AMD's heavier reliance on PC gaming, a market it says has been hurt by supply constraints on gaming GPUs. On top of that, AMD has openly admitted that demand is running ahead of what it can ship, and Lisa Su recently called AMD a "data center first" company.Intel's gain probably says more about supply than about its desktop chips suddenly winning over gamers. Mercury notes that desktop volumes took a large hit in Q2, and both companies saw mobile CPU shipments drop by more than 10% in Q3. In servers, the trend went the other way, with AMD rising to 35.5% from 34.5% the quarter before.

articles.title: Operation Endgame Takes Down Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC Servers, Seizes 6.4M Stolen Logins
articles.summary:
An international police operation took down servers behind Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC this week. Criminals used the three malware tools to gain access to computers, steal passwords, and launch ransomware attacks.
Police also seized about 6.4 million stolen logins belonging to more than 40,000 victims, according to Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA).
Gootloader is a loader: once on a computer, it could download other malware, especially ransomware. It spread through fake legal documents placed on hacked websites, often WordPress sites. Criminals used SEO poisoning to push those sites high in search results.
Gootloader has infected at least 25,000 computers worldwide since 2018, the U.S. Justice Department said. Its operators used those computers to infect more computers, then sold access to the new ones to ransomware criminals. In the U.S., Gootloader was used in ransomware attacks against at least 44 victims, resulting in about $28.8 million in losses.
German police gave a much higher count in their statement in German. Based on what investigators know so far, Gootloader has infected millions of computers worldwide since it first appeared in 2020.
Across the three tools, police seized 235 servers and 257 domains, according to an operation summary from Europol, which supported the action. The takedown is part of Operation Endgame, an international police campaign against malware criminals use to access victims' computers.

articles.title: SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
articles.summary:
A newly identified spying group used hacked equipment inside Asian mobile operators to intercept the calls and texts of selected people, mostly in Taiwan.
Enea, a telecom and cybersecurity software company based in Stockholm, found the group's attack sources in at least six Asian countries and named it SilentAir this week. It assessed with high confidence that SilentAir is a state-level actor, but linked its activity to China only with low confidence.
The company has told the operators where it found SilentAir sources. It said SilentAir has been disrupted for now but could return. The report does not say whether those operators have cleaned up the hacked equipment.
Mobile operators use the SS7 and Diameter protocols to exchange signaling messages that route calls and texts and enable roaming. This traffic crosses a shared network called the IPX, which runs on a high level of trust between operators. SilentAir sent its attacks into the IPX from the hacked equipment.
For interception, SilentAir sent the target's home network an UpdateLocation message, or its Diameter equivalent. The message claimed that the hacked equipment was now serving the target's phone. If the home network accepted it, calls and texts for that person would be diverted to the attackers.

articles.title: When an AI Agent Goes Wrong, Can You Stop It?
articles.summary:
Suppose an AI agent is asked to sort support tickets and look up account details. A ticket contains instructions that lead the agent to export records to an unfamiliar destination. The agent can make the request because its identity has access to the records and its connected tools allow the action.
That kind of scenario raises a response question: what does “stop the agent” actually mean? A team may be able to pause the model while a workflow, credential or existing connection remains active. Those pieces can require separate controls.
An October 2026 roundup from the OWASP GenAI Security Project describes evaluation agents reaching beyond their intended scope and recommends testing whether containment can revoke both credentials and network access. The roundup is a selected collection, not an exhaustive survey of incidents.
Turning off the model may not stop the work
An AI agent is usually part of a larger system. A model may choose an action, but an orchestrator runs the workflow, an identity supplies access and tools or APIs carry out the work. Network rules determine where those tools can connect.
The details vary by deployment. In one system, disabling the agent may stop its current task. In another, queued jobs, retries or an already established session may continue. Revoking one credential may not invalidate a different token or connection. A model endpoint can be offline while a separate service continues to process work it already received.

Three Trezor Safe 5 wallets bought from the reseller CryptoBilis contain an implant, an extra circuit board that can copy their recovery phrases, hardware wallet maker Trezor said yesterday.
The implant reads the phrase from the wallet's screen and sends it over the mobile network to a server controlled by the attackers. The company examined one of the wallets in its lab, identified the other two from photos their owners sent, and has had no reports of lost funds.
A firmware update released earlier this week, version 2.13.1, stops the implants found so far from capturing anything on wallets that run it, the company said, but “the update can’t protect a wallet backup that was captured before it.”
The company has not changed its advice to anyone who bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis since March, including from the reseller's stores on Tokopedia and Shopee:
- Move your funds to a new wallet with a new recovery phrase. Restoring the old phrase on another wallet does not solve the problem.
- Do not set up an unused wallet from the reseller, and never type an existing recovery phrase into one.
- Keep the wallet and contact Trezor Support, which offers a new Trezor wallet to anyone who bought from the reseller since March. Contact Support too if you are not sure where your wallet came from.
- Do not weigh or open the wallet to check it. Neither is a reliable test.

FAA grounds all US flights due to 'telecommunication outage' — officials say ' no indication...that this was a nefarious attack,' but they can't rule out a cyberattack yet
Every flight called back home — check your travel apps
For only the third time in 25 years, the FAA has called a ground stop for all air traffic in the US. US officials said a telecommunications issue has hampered Air Traffic Control Centers across the US and their ability to communicate with planes in the air.

articles.title: New Mior and Skyfall Attacks Let Rogue Cloud Hosts Steal Secrets From AMD SEV-SNP VMs
articles.summary:
Two attacks made public this week allow a malicious host to read data inside AMD SEV-SNP-protected virtual machines (VMs), which are built to keep the server's operator out.
One of them, Mior, can also modify a VM's memory and fake the signed report confirming which software it runs. Both need control of the server's hypervisor, and Mior also needs control of the server's BIOS. Researchers showed both in lab tests on AMD EPYC server processors.
AMD, which makes the processors, lists SEV firmware for Mior and microcode for Skyfall, both dated August 12. It plans to give server makers platform firmware in November for Skyfall and in December for Mior, and fixes for embedded chips later. Customers are told to get the BIOS update from their server maker.
SEV-SNP brings confidential computing to AMD EPYC server processors. It uses hardware-enforced memory encryption and access control to protect a VM, even from the host's hypervisor.
The ETH Zurich team behind Mior attacked SEV-SNP while it was starting up. During start-up, a security co-processor on the chip, the Platform Security Processor (PSP), fills in a table called the Reverse Map Table (RMP). The RMP records who owns each page of memory and what they may do with it.

articles.title: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Flaws, Including 22-Year-Old Bug Enabling Authenticated RCE
articles.summary:
A type confusion flaw in PostgreSQL lets a database user who can create objects run code on the server. Updates released yesterday fix it, along with 51 other security flaws. Full protection from this flaw also requires rebuilding any C-language extensions installed on the server.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-6460, has a CVSS score of 8.8. Any code run this way has the rights of the operating system user that runs PostgreSQL. All versions before 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.
The PostgreSQL Global Development Group, which publishes the database's releases, has not reported any attacks using the flaw. CISA's assessment in the CVE record also lists exploitation as none.
The flaw involves composite types, which are types built from named fields, each with its own data type. A field's type can be changed while older values of that type are still held in other parts of the server.
The server could then read an old value as if it had the new type. The fix, described in the project's release notes, adds version checks so the server can detect a value that no longer matches its type.
Security researcher Mehmet Ince described a working exploit for the flaw, demonstrated on PostgreSQL 18.6, in a technical writeup published this week.

En su lugar, ofrece las llaves de acceso (passkeys) y el correo electrónico verificado. Al iniciar sesión, el usuario verá la opción “Sign in faster” (“Iniciar sesión más rápido”) para crear una llave de acceso. Qué son las llaves de acceso y por qué reemplazan al SMS
Una llave de acceso permite entrar a una cuenta con la huella, el reconocimiento facial o el PIN del dispositivo, sin escribir contraseña ni código. Según Microsoft, es un método resistente al phishing —engaño para robar datos mediante mensajes o páginas falsas— y más rápido que el SMS.
La empresa afirma que el SMS es vulnerable al phishing y a los ataques de duplicado de la tarjeta SIM, en los que un delincuente consigue controlar el número de teléfono de la víctima, y lo describe como uno de los métodos más usados para tomar el control de cuentas ajenas.

articles.title: Estas funciones tecnológicas de seguridad en carros evitan choques y vigilan los puntos ciegos
articles.summary:
Las funciones tecnológicas de los vehículos actuales tienen un foco creciente en la seguridad. Los sistemas de asistencia buscan advertir riesgos, apoyar las maniobras y, en algunos casos, intervenir para reducir la posibilidad de una colisión.
El Cupra León VZ y el Cupra Terramar PHEV incorporan herramientas orientadas a prevenir impactos y a asistir al conductor en el control del vehículo.
El Volkswagen Golf GTI, que llegará a Colombia en 2027, suma funciones como Side Assist para supervisar los puntos ciegos durante los cambios de carril.
Estas tecnologías no reemplazan la atención de quien conduce, pero amplían su capacidad para detectar vehículos, peatones, ciclistas u otras situaciones que pueden pasar inadvertidas.
Cómo funcionan Front Assist y Pre-Crash de Cupra
El Front Assist de Cupra es un asistente de colisión frontal con frenado de emergencia.
Su función es identificar situaciones en las que el vehículo se aproxima a un obstáculo o a otro automóvil y existe riesgo de impacto. Ante esa posibilidad, el sistema puede advertir al conductor y activar el frenado de emergencia.
Esta tecnología está presente en el Cupra León VZ y en el Cupra Terramar PHEV. Su objetivo es apoyar la reacción del conductor en momentos en los que el tiempo disponible para responder puede ser limitado.
A este sistema se suma Pre-Crash, una función de precolisión que prepara el vehículo ante una situación de riesgo.

articles.title: Test iPhone Duo : trois semaines avec le premier pliant d'Apple, entre coup de cœur et frustrations
articles.summary:
On voulait un iPhone pliant pour profiter d’un grand écran sans quitter nos habitudes Apple. Depuis sa sortie le 23 octobre, le Duo a pris la place de notre Pro Max, et franchement, on n’a pas envie de le rendre. Reste qu’à 2 339 €, Touch ID, la photo et une bonne partie de nos applications nous ont donné quelques raisons de râler.
On ne va pas se mentir, si l’on attendait un iPhone pliant depuis des années, c’était davantage par envie que par besoin. Quand on baigne dans la tech depuis quinze ans, on finit par espérer autre chose qu’un nouveau placement des objectifs ou les trois couleurs de l’année. On veut retrouver un peu d’excitation en découvrant un téléphone, avoir envie de jouer avec, de voir ce qu’il permet. Alors quand Apple promet enfin un grand écran qui se replie dans la poche, sans quitter nos applications ni nos habitudes, forcément, on a hâte de l’avoir entre les mains.
- Fabrication et charnière remarquables
- Format passeport très agréable
- Écran mat nano-texturé, pliure discrète
- Excellents haut-parleurs
- Puissance au niveau de l’iPhone 18 Pro
- Autonomie confortable
- Certification IP68
- Applications et jeux encore rarement adaptés
- Bande latérale mal exploitée, rien pour les gauchers
- Touch ID moins efficace que Face ID
- Pas de téléobjectif, photo moins constante en basse lumière
- Lourd en main quand il est fermé
- Pas de Siri AI en Europe
Test réalisé sur un smartphone prêté par le constructeur.

articles.title: Avast VPN gratuit : données illimitées, mais trois choix de lieux définitifs
articles.summary:
Avast VPN est désormais disponible gratuitement en France. Le service offre des données illimitées dans le cadre d’un usage raisonnable, le tout sur un nombre illimité d’appareils. Une proposition rare, qui mérite que l’on s’y intéresse afin de comprendre les mécaniques de l’offre.
Après s’être fait connaître grâce à son antivirus gratuit, Avast va plus loin en proposant un VPN accessible sans frais. Or, on le sait, quand le mot « gratuit » est associé à un VPN, cela a souvent tendance à cacher des limitations très restrictives. Qu’en est-il donc d’Avast VPN ? On fait le point.
Un VPN gratuit sans plafond mensuel de données
Avast VPN ne nécessite le paiement d’aucun abonnement. Pour commencer à l’utiliser, il suffit de créer un compte avec une adresse e-mail et un mot de passe. Sur Windows et macOS, le service est intégré à Avast One. Sur Android et iOS, il prend la forme d’une application Avast VPN dédiée.
Contrairement à d’autres VPN gratuits, celui d’Avast ne fixe pas de quota mensuel, dans le cadre d’un usage raisonnable. La navigation, les téléchargements et le streaming ne sont donc pas coupés au bout de quelques gigaoctets utilisés.
Le même compte peut être utilisé sur un nombre illimité d’ordinateurs, de smartphones et de tablettes compatibles. Il suffit d’installer l’application, puis de se connecter avec les mêmes identifiants. articles.title: Les créateurs d’un malware affirment que leur logiciel garde accès à Gmail même après un changement de mot de passe
articles.summary:
Les vendeurs de l'infostealer Remus Stealer promettent à leurs clients de lire votre boîte Gmail, même après un changement de votre mot de passe. Hudson Rock, une entreprise israélienne spécialisée dans les logiciels voleurs de données, a enquêté sur cette offre à 1 000 dollars par mois sans parvenir à confirmer cette promesse.
Pendant que la planète a le regard tourné sur la panne géante qui touche Microsoft et notamment son client de messagerie Outlook, Remus sévit sur Gmail. Remus, c'est un infostealer, un logiciel conçu pour copier en quelques secondes les mots de passe et les cookies de connexion enregistrés dans votre navigateur. Avec un cookie volé, un pirate ouvre votre compte sans mot de passe ni code de vérification. Mais lorsque vous changez votre mot de passe Google, l’entreprise invalide en général les jetons de connexion encore actifs, et le pirate perd l’accès à votre compte. Dans l’annonce de la version 1.3.9 de Remus, ses développeurs affirment intercepter vos codes de vérification par e-mail sans voler le moindre cookie, et garder l’accès à vos messages après un changement de mot de passe et la révocation de vos sessions.
Les clients de Remus lisent votre boîte Gmail depuis leur tableau de bord
